#5032. Prop Firm Payouts Near $2 Billion: 10 Best Prop Firms In 2026

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Prop firm payouts are approaching the $2 billion mark, with data from Payout Junction showing nearly $1.97 billion in cumulative payments across 45 tracked firms since October 2023. More than $115 million has been recorded in November 2026 alone.

The figures offer a glimpse into how large the funded trading industry has become. But finding the best prop firms in 2026 requires looking at something payout leaderboards rarely tell you: what traders actually have to go through to get paid.

A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown gives a trader just $3,000 of room for error. Add consistency requirements, withdrawal caps and restrictions on trading strategies, and two accounts with identical advertised balances can offer very different trading conditions.

The industry is also expanding beyond its traditional forex and futures markets. New platforms are introducing prop trading for cryptocurrencies and tokenized stocks, giving traders access to a wider range of markets without having to commit the full advertised account balance themselves.

For this guide, we examine ten prop firms across forex, futures and cryptocurrency markets, looking beyond advertised profit splits to compare evaluation rules, trading conditions, costs and payout eligibility.

Editorial disclosure: This guide is based on published trading rules, product documentation and available payout data. Traders can lose their challenge fees, and most retail funded trading programs initially use simulated accounts. Receiving a payout is not guaranteed.

The firms are grouped by their suitability for different trading styles rather than ranked by a single payout leaderboard.

According to Payout Junction’s November 24 data, approximately 1.19 million payout transactions have been matched to public blockchain records since October 2023.

The tracker covers 45 firms, although its figures do not necessarily represent all payments made by those businesses. Bank transfers and other payments outside its blockchain tracking coverage may not appear in the dataset.

November has already recorded roughly $115.5 million in tracked payments across more than 91,000 transactions.

These are substantial figures, but they need context.

A firm paying out $50 million does not necessarily offer a better opportunity than one paying out $5 million. The larger business could simply have more customers, higher fees or a larger number of accounts.

Chart by NewsBTC, data from Payout Junction, November 16–22, 2026. Tracked blockchain payments only.

Nor do the figures tell us how much traders collectively spent on challenges, resets and subscriptions before receiving those payouts.

Without that information, it is impossible to determine the industry’s aggregate profitability for traders.

Payout data is useful evidence that payments have occurred. It is not evidence that the average customer makes money.

That distinction matters when comparing the following firms.

FTMO offers a conventional two-phase evaluation for traders who prefer clearly defined profit objectives and fixed overall loss limits.

Its two-step model requires a 10% profit target during the first phase and 5% during verification.

The maximum daily loss is 5% of the initial simulated capital, while the overall loss limit is 10%.

For a $100,000 evaluation, that translates into a $10,000 first-phase profit target and a $10,000 maximum overall loss allowance.

FTMO also offers a separate one-step model. Traders should not assume that its rules are identical to the traditional challenge.

The two-step structure may appeal to traders whose strategies require more breathing room than accounts with narrow trailing loss limits.

The first-phase target, however, requires meaningful performance relative to the allowed drawdown.

FTMO is worth considering for traders with an existing, tested forex or CFD strategy. Its two-step structure is easier to assess mathematically than many trailing-drawdown alternatives, although that does not make it easy to pass.

FundedNext operates across CFDs and futures, offering several routes to funded-style trading.

Its Stellar 2-Step model is particularly interesting for traders who want a traditional evaluation with relatively conventional risk limits.

The first phase requires an 8% return, followed by 5% in verification. Both phases apply a 5% daily loss limit and 10% maximum overall loss.

The published rules specify five minimum trading days per phase.

The firm also offers alternative CFD challenge formats and futures evaluations.

One area worth examining is its performance reward policy. Reward frequency and eligibility can vary according to the option selected, with some routes requiring a specific number of profitable trading days.

This makes comparing the headline profit split alone insufficient.

FundedNext’s strongest feature is choice. Its biggest complication is also choice. Traders should compare the funded-stage conditions of each product before deciding which evaluation to purchase.

FundingPips offers several evaluation models, including one-step, two-step and evaluation-free alternatives.

Its 2-Step Standard model requires an 8% profit target followed by 5% in verification.

The firm’s current documentation also confirms that the previous optional 10% first-phase target was discontinued on July 24, 2026.

FundingPips is an example of why traders must pay attention to changes in prop firm rules.

Its Standard model documentation applies a 35% consistency condition to the on-demand reward cycle.

This means a trader who generates most of their profit during one unusually successful session could need additional trading before qualifying for a withdrawal.

That might suit a strategy producing relatively steady returns. It could be less suitable for traders whose profits are concentrated around a handful of strong market opportunities.

FundingPips deserves consideration for its payout flexibility, but traders should examine the conditions attached to their preferred withdrawal cycle rather than choosing whichever option advertises the highest reward share.

The5ers offers several forex-focused evaluation and account-development programs.

Its High Stakes program is built around a two-stage evaluation and subsequent growth opportunities.

The firm distinguishes between different versions of High Stakes, making it important to identify the exact account being purchased rather than relying on older comparisons.

The appeal of The5ers is its focus on account development over time.

Traders who already have a strategy capable of producing steady returns may find growth-oriented programs more interesting than accounts designed primarily around rapid evaluations.

However, scaling opportunities should not be treated as guaranteed increases in accessible trading capital.

The trader must meet the conditions attached to the program, and trading restrictions continue to apply.

The5ers is a reasonable candidate for patient forex traders who value gradual account development. Its suitability depends on the precise High Stakes version and the trader’s ability to satisfy its growth criteria.

Hola Prime offers multiple evaluation formats across forex, CFDs and futures.

Its 2-Step Prime challenge requires an 8% profit target during the first phase and 5% during the second, with at least three trading days in each phase.

The firm’s published schedules also differentiate risk limits according to account size.

Hola Prime’s product range gives traders alternatives to the standard evaluation experience. However, account fees, platform access and withdrawal terms differ across models.

Its advertised challenge-fee refund also comes with conditions. Under the reviewed 2-Step Prime terms, the refund is distributed across the first four successful payouts rather than returned immediately upon passing.

That is an important detail for anyone calculating how much they need to earn before recovering their initial expenses.

Hola Prime is worth comparing if trading platform choice matters to you. Just remember that a fast payout-processing promise begins after a withdrawal becomes eligible, not necessarily after your first profitable trade.

Topstep is focused on futures trading through its Trading Combine and subsequent funded-account structure.

Unlike a traditional CFD evaluation, the maximum loss allowance is relatively small compared with the advertised account size.

Its published Trading Combine parameters include maximum loss limits of $2,000 for a $50,000 account, $3,000 for a $100,000 account and $4,500 for a $150,000 account.

A trader purchasing the $50,000 option is not receiving $50,000 that can be lost while testing a strategy. The relevant initial risk allowance is $2,000.

After passing the Trading Combine, traders can progress to an Express Funded Account, which is a simulated funded-stage account.

Its payout policy includes conditions relating to withdrawal eligibility, payout limits and changes to the maximum loss threshold after withdrawals.

Topstep is worth considering for futures traders who prefer a structured environment. Anyone moving from forex prop trading should first understand how dollar-based trailing loss limits differ from percentage-based static drawdowns.

Tradeify offers futures evaluations with different routes into funded-stage trading.

Its Select evaluation does not impose a daily loss limit during the evaluation but does apply a consistency requirement.

After passing, traders choose between Select Flex and Select Daily payout policies.

The ability to select a payout arrangement is attractive because not every trader earns profits in the same way.

A trader producing relatively consistent daily returns may prefer a different structure from someone whose strategy depends on occasional larger moves.

However, the choice is permanent for that funded account, according to Tradeify’s official payout policy.

Changing to the alternative arrangement requires obtaining another qualifying account.

Tradeify’s Select model is particularly interesting because it allows traders to choose how they want to approach withdrawals after evaluation. That flexibility is only valuable if the trader understands both options before selecting one.

Take Profit Trader offers futures trading programs built around an evaluation, a simulated PRO account and potential progression to a live-market PRO+ account.

The firm published updated plan information on November 23, 2026, making older descriptions of its account rules particularly important to recheck.

Its current product announcement describes three-day evaluations, frequent PRO withdrawals and no funded-stage consistency rule under the new plans.

The buffer is the detail traders should examine most closely.

The firm allows eligible traders to withdraw profits above the required buffer. Consequently, a trader can have a profitable account without necessarily being able to withdraw all that profit while retaining the account.

Legacy accounts may also remain subject to their original terms.

Take Profit Trader stands out for its withdrawal model. Traders interested in frequent payouts should still calculate how much profit must remain in the account before treating those earnings as spendable income.

Lucid Trading offers several futures account models, including LucidPro, LucidFlex, LucidDirect and LucidDaily.

Its LucidFlex program is particularly relevant to traders who want to avoid funded-stage profit-concentration restrictions.

According to the firm’s LucidFlex documentation, the funded account does not impose a consistency rule or a separate payout buffer.

The published profit-sharing arrangement is 90% for the trader.

The absence of a consistency rule does not mean traders can withdraw unrestricted amounts whenever they choose.

LucidFlex still has specific payout conditions, including requirements that must be satisfied before a withdrawal is approved.

Traders must also consider how a payout affects the account’s maximum loss threshold.

LucidFlex may appeal to traders who dislike having their profitable sessions constrained by a consistency formula. That makes the account more flexible in one respect, not necessarily less risky overall.

HyroTrader focuses on cryptocurrency traders rather than adapting a traditional forex evaluation to include a limited selection of digital assets.

Its one-step program requires a 10% profit target, with a 4% daily drawdown and 6% maximum overall loss under the published model.

The firm also offers alternative evaluation formats, including its recently introduced lower-cost Hyro Core program.

The attraction is that traders can use crypto-oriented trading infrastructure and market data rather than relying exclusively on a conventional forex platform.

For traders unfamiliar with derivatives, our guide to long and short positions in crypto explains how leverage and liquidation affect market exposure.

HyroTrader’s trading rules also clarify that allocated challenge and funded-account balances are simulated. Payouts represent a contractual share of eligible simulated trading performance.

That distinction matters because the term funded account is frequently misunderstood.

HyroTrader is worth examining for traders who already specialize in crypto markets. It is less compelling for someone whose only reason for choosing crypto is the belief that higher volatility makes a challenge easier to pass.

There is no single account structure that suits everyone.

These selections reflect specific published product features, not independently measured payout approval rates or guarantees of superior results.

The advertised account balance is usually one of the least informative numbers in a prop firm comparison.

Account A offers twice the advertised balance of Account B. Yet it provides less room for losses and requires a substantially higher profit relative to that allowance.

This does not establish the probability of passing either challenge. That depends on the strategy, trading costs, risk management and other account rules.

It does show why choosing the largest advertised account is not always sensible.

The calculation becomes more complicated when an account uses trailing drawdown.

A static maximum loss threshold remains anchored to a specified balance under the account’s rules.

A trailing drawdown moves upward as the trader generates profits, potentially reducing the room available for a subsequent losing streak.

Intraday trailing drawdown is particularly important because some models adjust the threshold based on unrealized profits.

A trade that briefly gains $1,000 before closing with a much smaller profit can therefore affect the trader’s remaining loss allowance.

Two firms advertising the same maximum drawdown can offer very different practical conditions depending on how and when that threshold moves.

Passing an evaluation is generally only the first stage.

The rules that determine whether someone receives a withdrawal can be more restrictive than the initial profit targets.

A consistency rule limits how much of the qualifying profit can come from a single trading session or another defined period.

For example, suppose a trader earns $2,000 during their best day and finishes the payout cycle with $4,000 in qualifying profit.

That best day represents 50% of the total.

Under a hypothetical 40% consistency requirement, total qualifying profit would need to reach at least $5,000, assuming the best day remains unchanged and the rule uses this particular calculation.

The trader may have to continue trading even though they are already profitable.

Some firms require profits to remain in an account as a buffer against future losses.

Others limit how much traders can withdraw during their initial payout cycles.

These restrictions are not necessarily unreasonable. A firm may want traders to demonstrate sustained performance before allowing larger withdrawals.

But customers should know exactly what they are buying.

There is a considerable difference between advertising daily payouts and allowing a trader to withdraw every dollar earned that day.

Account agreements can restrict copy trading, certain automated strategies, cross-account hedging, account sharing, news trading and other trading behaviors.

The precise definitions differ between firms.

Before paying for an account, traders should review both the public trading objectives and the account agreement governing payout eligibility.

A strategy permitted during evaluation may have different conditions after funding.

The advertised challenge price is only the initial expense.

Depending on the firm and product, customers may also incur subscription charges, reset fees, funded-account activation fees, market-data fees, platform costs or withdrawal-processing charges.

Promotional discounts can make the first purchase attractive without necessarily reducing the cost of subsequent attempts.

Consider a hypothetical trader who purchases four $100 challenges before successfully qualifying for a funded account. That trader has spent $400 before accounting for any additional charges.

The first $300 payout would not mean the trader has made a net profit from prop trading.

Their total challenge expenditure would still exceed their withdrawals.

This is another reason the industry’s approaching $2 billion payout milestone should not be confused with $2 billion in net trader earnings.

Our editorial assessment considers the following factors:

The selection is based on documentary research rather than a claim that NewsBTC has personally purchased, traded or withdrawn money from every program.

Reported payouts are considered supporting evidence of industry activity, not a standalone measure of reliability.

Retail prop firms generally offer traders access to an evaluation or simulated trading program in exchange for a fee.

Belgium’s financial regulator, the FSMA, has also published a consumer warning about retail prop trading programs, highlighting the risks of paying for repeated challenges.

Participants who meet the contractual requirements may receive monetary rewards linked to their trading performance. Some businesses subsequently move qualifying traders into live-market accounts.

This is different from opening a conventional brokerage account with personal deposited trading capital.

It also means traders should examine who operates the program, which legal entity they contract with, where disputes are handled and what happens if the provider changes its rules or ceases operations.

A large number of successful payout transactions does not guarantee that every valid withdrawal will be approved, nor does it establish the financial health of the company.

Before buying a challenge, traders should read the current agreement, establish their eligibility and understand which circumstances can lead to account termination.

FTMO and FundedNext are worth comparing for traditional forex evaluations. Topstep, Tradeify, Take Profit Trader and Lucid Trading offer different futures trading structures, while HyroTrader is focused on cryptocurrency.

The most suitable firm depends on the trader’s strategy, risk tolerance, market preference and withdrawal requirements.

Take Profit Trader offers daily eligible withdrawals under its reviewed PRO model, subject to the required buffer. Tradeify also offers a Select Daily payout arrangement.

Daily availability does not remove other eligibility conditions.

LucidFlex does not impose a funded-stage consistency rule under its published terms. Take Profit Trader’s new PRO plans also advertise no funded-stage consistency requirement.

Evaluation-stage restrictions may still apply.

HyroTrader is one of the crypto-focused firms worth researching because its programs are built around digital-asset trading.

Traders should compare cryptocurrency market access, drawdown calculations, exchange integrations and payout eligibility before selecting a program.

Yes. Traders can lose evaluation fees, subscriptions, reset fees and other charges without ever receiving a payout.

The simulated nature of many funded accounts does not eliminate the financial risk of paying for repeated evaluations.

No. Withdrawals depend on the firm’s contractual requirements, trading-rule compliance and ability to make payments.

Historical payout figures do not guarantee future withdrawals.

The prop trading industry has grown considerably, and nearly $2 billion in tracked payouts demonstrates that substantial sums are changing hands.

What it does not demonstrate is how many traders are profitable after accounting for their expenses.

The best prop firm is not necessarily the one paying the most money, offering the largest account or advertising the highest profit split.

It is the one whose evaluation and funded-stage rules are compatible with a trader’s existing strategy.

Before purchasing a challenge, calculate how much room the account actually provides for losses, how much profit must be generated before a withdrawal becomes possible and how much repeated attempts could cost.

Those numbers are considerably more useful than the advertised account balance.

#5031. Tether Gold Under Pressure: Bitcoin and Gold Losses Erase 70% of USDT’s Cushion

Falling gold and Bitcoin prices erase an estimated $5.7 billion from Tether’s holdings, putting its USDT reserve cushion under pressure.

Gold just slid toward $3,500 an ounce and silver fell below $40, extending a sell-off that has put Tether gold back in focus. Why? Tether keeps billions of dollars of gold bars in the reserves behind USDT, so the crash hits its balance sheet directly.

Based on Tether’s latest reserves report and the blockchain, the company holds about 168 tons of gold: 142.8 tons it owns in its USDT reserves, plus 25.7 tons backing its Tether Gold (XAUT) token.

Gold just crashed below $3,500 and silver below $40, hitting their lowest levels in almost 15 months.

$1.2 TRILLION has been wiped out from gold and silver in the last 24 hours. pic.twitter.com/7OLr78DM1N

— Bull Theory (@BullTheoryio) November 25, 2026

USDT, meanwhile, is shrinking. Its supply has fallen $16 billion from its May peak.

Although Bitcoin has recently reclaimed the $60,000 price mark after seeing a sudden shift in market sentiments that triggered increases of over 6% in its price during the last day, momentum has slowed again, further stretching the prolonged volatility seen over the past months.

With the Bitcoin bear market still persisting, Grayscale has sparked discussions across the crypto market after drawing attention toward a major bearish milestone for the asset.

Earlier today, Grayscale revealed that Bitcoin's current bear market has lasted more than 411 days and is becoming the longest on record.

While this marks an historic milestone in the Bitcoin bear market, Grayscale further disclosed an interesting twist that makes the current bear market pretty different from previous times.

The source confirmed that this bear market has been relatively mild in terms of price losses despite lasting longer than previous downturns.

All through the current bear market, Bitcoin has only posted a price decrease 56%, suggesting that it has suffered considerably smaller losses than several previous bear markets.

This means that even though Bitcoin has spent more than a year in a bear market, its decline has not been as severe as those seen in earlier cycles.

To back the data, Grayscale showed charts comparing Bitcoin's performance across historical bear markets that ended in June 2011, December 2013, December 2017, November 2021, and the ongoing October 2025 cycle.

While the 2011, 2017 and 2021 bear cycles suffered massive losses, especially during the former when its indexed performance fell below 10, the current 2025 bear market broke historical pattern by enduring a longer period yet a comparatively modest decline in Bitcoin’s price.

#5029. Does South Korea’s draft bill give banks control of won-backed stablecoins?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The South Korean FSC’s new draft bill could change things for the country’s crypto space. What’s what’s going on exactly?

Under the new plan, banks put together can own more than half of any won stablecoin issuer. A fintech company can still be the largest shareholder, but they can’t run the show alone anymore.

Issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity. Reserves must cover 100% of tokens in circulation, and holders must be able to cash out at face value right away.

As far as exchanges go, one shareholder can hold 20% or 34% with FSC approval. They’ll also need separate licences for dealing, brokerage, and custody.

South Korea’s plan is a 22% tax on crypto gains above 2.5 million won a year. It was meant to kick in this January, but it looks like that date’s been pushed back to 2029.

One reason is that it’s the earliest Korea can start swapping crypto tax data with the United States.

If that happens, it won’t be the first delay. The tax was first proposed back in 2020 and has been shelved several times since.

Enforcement is still active though. AMBCrypto previously reported that 27 unlicensed exchange websites were blocked recently, including KuCoin, MEXC and BingX. This was after their apps were already restricted.

Users on those platforms are being nudged towards the country’s 28 licensed exchanges.

#5027. Saylor Spots New Role for Bitcoin

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor sees new ways to put Bitcoin (BTC) to work on Wall Street.

According to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S. derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses.

‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov. 23.

As per the guidance, these companies must maintain sufficient financial resources to cover their operating costs for at least a year.

As clarified by CFTC staff, Bitcoin and Ether can be used to meet this requirement (as well as payment stablecoins). The advisory also provides guidance on how staff interpret the current rules. It also applies to swap execution facilities (SEFs), which are platforms where counterparties trade swaps.

Bitcoin holdings worth $10 million could count for $8 million toward the annual requirement, based on the minimum 20% discount that CFTC staff said they would accept. This provides some flexibility in case Bitcoin's price falls. The discount is also called a haircut.

For Ether, the same minimum 20% haircut applies. For payment stablecoins, the haircut is 2%.

This provides some incentive for an exchange to actually hold BTC. Exchanges could hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets and use some of its value to satisfy this reserve requirement. There would be no need to sell it for USD first.

However, a futures exchange still needs to have sufficient unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities to cover its operating costs for at least six months. Bitcoin, Ether and even payment stablecoins do not fall into this category.

The same six-month liquidity requirement applies to clearinghouses. Additionally, they need to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover a default by a clearing member.

CFTC staff also noted a potential downside for exchanges holding crypto reserves. During a market slump, there's a risk that an exchange's operating losses might rise. At the same time, the value of the Bitcoin it holds to cover those losses might fall.

So this possibility should be considered before an exchange decides whether to use Bitcoin to meet its financial resource requirements.

#5026. Top 8 Decentralised Exchanges to look out for in November 2026

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Decentralised exchanges, or DEXs, use smart contracts or liquidity pools to facilitate cryptocurrency trading. Users are at the core of DEXs, as they retain complete control over their assets and do not need to depend on centralized exchanges to protect their funds or process their withdrawals. DEXs let users maintain ownership of their private keys and also reduce the risk of custody failures.

Here is our list of the top 8 decentralized exchanges in the space that users can trade on:

Pancake or PancakeSwap is one of the most popular DEXs on the BNB Chain and was created to provide users with a low-cost, accessible alternative to Ethereum-based decentralized exchanges.

The platform recently rebranded from PancakeSwap to Pancake, dropping “Swap” as it expanded from a single-chain token-swap DEX to a multi-chain liquidity hub spanning 11+ blockchains, and added perpetual futures and 24/7 tokenized stocks and ETFs.

Uniswap introduced the Automated Market Maker (AMM) model that changed how cryptocurrency trading could take place without any central intermediaries or traditional order books. Users could swap tokens directly from their wallets across Ethereum and other blockchains.

The platform also allows users to earn rewards through peer-to-peer trading, and the open-source architecture has influenced others in the space, making it an important reference point for the DEX industry.

Raydium leverages Solana’s high-speed blockchain infrastructure, combining AMM, liquidity infrastructure, and token trading functionality. This is useful not just for DeFi users but also for retail users.

Users can trade and exchange their assets directly through their wallets. The tools on Raydium help new projects establish liquidity and attract traders. RAY is the native token of the platform and is useful with governance and incentives on the platform.

Hyperliquid has an order book that runs on-chain instead of an AMM, giving users a centralized experience. The platform is especially known for its perpetual futures and spot trading services, whereas the ecosystem itself supports borrowing, lending, and real-world assets.

The platform is a Layer 1 chain and consists of 2 main components: HyperCore and HyperEVM. HyperBFT is the consensus mechanism used underneath to support both. Stop, limit, and margin orders are all supported on Hyperliquid. HYPE is the native token of the platform.

Balancer is a DEX protocol built on Ethereum that supports multi-token liquidity pools and yield-bearing assets. Token pairings can be customized with multiple assets, unlike the traditional 50/50 pairings. It functions more like an automated portfolio manager, customizing token weights, creating pools with adjustable weight ratios, and letting users set their own trading fee.

The platform provides a level of flexibility that lets users and liquidity providers create specialized trading environments and program them as per their needs.

SushiSwap was launched as a fork of Uniswap in 2020 and lets users trade through liquidity pools instead of traditional order books. These users can either be Traders or Swappers or users who want to exchange one cryptocurrency for another; or Liquidity Providers who supply assets to liquidity pools to conduct trades.

The platform uses a multichain approach and supports various blockchain networks, letting users access different DeFi environments. The native token of the platform is SUSHI, which is useful in governance and incentive-based applications.

Orca lets users swap and conduct transactions at lightning fast speeds. Whirlpools are the platform’s concentrated liquidity pools that let liquidity providers provide capital within selected price ranges instead of distributing it uniformly across a price curve.

Orca is the native token of the platform. The platform’s simple interface appeals to a lot of traders. Wallet-to-wallet trading of SPL tokens is also a viable option for users.

Meteora is a liquidity protocol built on Solana focusing on providing advanced liquidity management and supporting token swaps. Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker or DLMM is a major feature of the platform allowing liquidity providers to allocate assets across different price bins.

Liquidity providers get to concentrate their assets around selected trading prices and various liquidity pool configurations can accomodate various market conditions and trading strategies. Meteora also supports emerging token projects and liquidity tools that can be helpful to establish trading markets and manage liquidity.

Decentralised exchanges are an essential part of the crypto and DeFi ecosystem. DEX platforms give users an extra level of control over their assets when they buy, sell, exchange or manage their assets.

While every trader has their own requirements, the best platform would depend upon individual needs, preferred networks, trading pairs and risks. Users should do their own research before investing.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Each account trading on the XRP Ledger's decentralized exchange moved an average of 4,328 XRP a day in the third quarter of 2026, up 437% from 805 XRP in the same quarter a year earlier, according to a report that XRP treasury company Evernorth released on Tuesday.

According to Evernorth, the average swap on the XRP Ledger reached 35 XRP in the third quarter, up from 19 XRP in the second quarter and under 6 XRP a year earlier. "The growth came from bigger trades, not more of them," the company wrote in the report.

At the same time, the number of accounts trading on the XRP Ledger's order book fell to 1,042 a day in the third quarter of 2026 from 2,027 a day in the third quarter of 2025. The number stood at 1,203 in the fourth quarter of 2025, 1,324 in the first quarter of 2026 and 1,125 in the second quarter, according to the report.

Order-book volume on the XRP Ledger rose to 4.51 million XRP a day in the third quarter from 1.63 million XRP a day a year earlier, Evernorth data shows.

In total, 5.16 million XRP a day was traded on the XRP Ledger's exchange in the third quarter, and the figure was up 96% year over year, according to Evernorth.

Measured in U.S. dollars, exchange volume on the XRP Ledger fell 15% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the report.

Evernorth also compared the XRP Ledger with Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche and Polygon. Across these seven networks, exchange volume in dollars fell 42% over the same period, the report shows.

XRP was trading at around $0.93 on Tuesday morning after reaching as high as $1.026 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap.

The report also shows that the average balance of Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger reached $937 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from $539 million in the second quarter. By the end of the quarter, the RLUSD balance on the XRP Ledger stood at $1.15 billion, compared with $670 million at the end of the second quarter, and the number of RLUSD holders on the network rose to 67,449 from 45,620.

According to Evernorth, the XRP Ledger's average share of RLUSD reached 48.5% in the third quarter, up from 34% in the second quarter. Still, Ethereum finished the quarter with more RLUSD than the XRP Ledger. Evernorth noted that on Ethereum, RLUSD "can already be lent," and that on the XRP Ledger, "native lending is in validator voting."

As of Nov. 20, the Lending Protocol amendment had 24 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. The amendment needs 29 votes, held for 14 days, to activate.

Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9, and its shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN on Oct. 12. The company entered the public markets holding approximately 473 million XRP, according to its press release.

Evernorth announced the deal in October 2025, with investments from SBI, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

#5024. HyroTrader Adds Hyro Core From $9 and No-Evaluation Hyro Instant to Rebuilt Crypto Prop Platform

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The new accounts follow an October overhaul that brought the firm’s own trading terminal, AI-agent trading, BloFin and static loss limits on every challenge

DUBAI, UAE, November 2026: HyroTrader, a crypto proprietary trading firm, has launched two new ways to get a funded trading account. Hyro Core is a one-phase challenge from $9, and Hyro Instant skips the challenge altogether. Both went on sale on 4 November 2026.

They are the second step of a rebuild that began in October. That month HyroTrader launched its own trading terminal with stock and index contracts and opened accounts on it to AI trading agents. It also added BloFin as a second exchange, made every loss limit static and made its payouts easier to verify on a public dashboard.

Firms like HyroTrader give traders a funded account and pay them a share of the profit made on it. Traders usually earn that account by passing a paid trading test, known as a challenge.

At HyroTrader, every account, funded or not, is a simulated (demo) account running on live market data. The payouts are real money, paid as a share of the simulated profit.

Hyro Instant is the bigger change for a firm that until now funded only traders who passed a challenge.

“Without an evaluation, a firm cannot establish whether a trader has a consistent track record or simply had a few successful trades,” HyroTrader said in announcing Hyro Instant. “Nevertheless, the demand for a faster route is clear.”

Hyro Core is the firm’s lowest-priced challenge. A $2,500 account costs $9, and the largest, $100,000, costs $349. Against One-Step, the firm’s other one-phase challenge, it pairs the lower price with tighter loss limits.

To pass, a trader needs a 10% profit over at least four trading days, with no single day counting for more than 40% of it. The challenge ends if the account loses more than 3% of its starting balance in a day, or 5% in total. Both limits are static, which means they stay fixed to the starting balance and do not rise as the account gains.

Funded Hyro Core traders receive a fixed 80% of the profit as payouts. The fee is not refunded once the challenge is activated.

“A trader’s budget does not necessarily reflect their motivation or skill,” HyroTrader said in announcing Hyro Core.

Hyro Instant, a funded account with no evaluation. Image: HyroTrader

Hyro Instant has no test at all. After identity verification and account setup, the trader receives a funded account with no profit target to reach. It costs from $169 for a $5,000 account to $2,799 for $100,000.

It keeps Hyro Core’s daily and total loss limits and adds a per-trade limit. No single trade may lose more than 2% of the starting balance. A first breach of that trade limit brings a warning, and a second closes the account.

The first payout opens after three qualifying trading days (days on which the trader closes at least one trade above set size and price-move thresholds), with the account in profit. The profit split starts at 80% and can rise to 90% at the firm’s discretion. The fee is refunded only if identity verification is not approved.

Both new accounts run on what HyroTrader built in October. At the centre is the Hyro platform, the firm’s own trading terminal, which needs no exchange account. It offers more than 700 perpetual futures markets (contracts with no expiry date) on live prices. Besides crypto, they include contracts on stocks such as Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, on the S&P 500, and on gold and silver.

Traders who prefer an exchange can instead run any programme on their own demo account at Bybit or, since October, at BloFin. HyroTrader says that in 2023 it became the first crypto prop firm to let traders run a challenge on their own exchange demo account.

On the Hyro platform, Hyro Instant accounts included, traders can also connect their own AI agent through MCP, the Model Context Protocol (an open standard for linking AI tools to other software). The agent places trades for the trader’s own strategy under the account’s usual rules, and the trader can revoke its access at any time.

The October rebuild also made payouts easier to check. HyroTrader lists the payouts it sends on the Solana blockchain on a public transparency page, each with a link to its blockchain record unless the trader has chosen to hide it. In November the minimum payout fell from $100 to $25.

The firm also eased its existing challenges in the same week. One-Step challenges bought from 5 November need at least three trading days instead of five and allow an 8% total loss limit instead of 6%. Two-Step challenges bought from 4 November need four trading days in each phase instead of five.

HyroTrader is a crypto prop firm launched in 2023 and operating from Dubai, UAE. Traders take a challenge or start funded with Hyro Instant, receive 80% of their profits as payouts, up to 90% on some programmes, and are usually paid in stablecoins within 24 hours.

According to HyroTrader’s public payout transparency page, the firm has paid more than $9.5 million in profit splits to traders since 2023, as of November 2026. More than $1.6 million of that went out on the Solana blockchain. HyroTrader says it has funded more than 1,700 traders.

HyroTrader is not a broker and does not provide investment services or advice. All trading takes place on simulated accounts.

#5021. Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided.

The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares.

The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum.

Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile.

Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services.

That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token.

This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular.

And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges.

Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins.

There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker.

The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust.

Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody.

That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market.

There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome.

First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away.

If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products.

Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.

#5020. LINK, AAVE and UNI Now Supported by Fidelity

Fidelity Investments now supports three new cryptocurrencies on its retail crypto trading platform: Chainlink (LINK), Aave (AAVE) and Uniswap (UNI).

The firm expanded from five available cryptocurrencies to eight on Nov. 24. In just one day, Fidelity added the same number of digital assets that it had added in the four years since it first made Bitcoin and Ether available for customer trading.

Eligible U.S. customers can trade these three tokens on the Fidelity website and app. Some states may have limited access to Fidelity's services.

Fidelity's three new listings include tokens that represent different areas of decentralized finance. Aave is a lending protocol where users can deposit crypto assets to earn interest or use them as collateral for loans. AAVE token holders can vote on changes to the protocol's lending markets and other aspects of its operation.

Uniswap is a decentralized trading platform where users can trade different tokens using shared pools of assets provided by other users. UNI is the Uniswap governance token.

Chainlink provides the data that blockchain apps need to operate. For example, a lending protocol might use a Chainlink price feed to assess the value of collateral for a borrower's loan. Chainlink (LINK) tokens are used to pay for services provided on its network.

Fidelity Crypto started accepting customers from its waitlist in November 2022. At the time, the only two cryptocurrencies it offered were Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH). By March 2023, Fidelity was offering its service to more eligible U.S. investors, but these were still the only cryptocurrencies it allowed customers to trade.

On July 17, 2024, Fidelity added Litecoin (LTC) to its list of cryptocurrencies, bringing the total to three. Over a year later, on Oct. 23, 2025, the company introduced Solana (SOL). In addition to individual retail accounts, Solana became available for crypto IRAs, wealth managers and institutional clients.

Fidelity added its fifth cryptocurrency on Feb. 4, 2026, when it launched Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD) as its first stablecoin available to retail and institutional investors. Eligible users can exchange or redeem each FIDD token for $1. Fidelity waives its usual crypto trading fee when users exchange FIDD for dollars.

#5019. Why Nvidia Needed Jensen Huang Back—And What His Return Really Changes

Why Nvidia Needed Jensen Huang Back—And What His Return Really Changes

Jensen Huang did not unveil a breakthrough chip on Monday. He simply got his old job back—and Nvidia shares surged more than 30%, while the Nasdaq jumped nearly 7% in midday trading.

The reaction revealed something more consequential than Wall Street’s fondness for a charismatic CEO: investors had spent 11 days confronting how much of the AI boom runs through one person.

Huang, who resigned November 12 amid revelations about extramarital affairs and an unproven Chinese espionage allegation involving a former customer executive, has returned as CEO, president, and director.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Nvidia’s board says his reinstatement poses no national security risk, based partly on input from senior U.S. officials. Its independent investigation, however, is not over.

The company did not stop making chips. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO, Harvey Jones took over as Nvidia’s first board chairman, and executives insisted the technology roadmap and customer commitments remained intact.

Kress presided over earnings that showed roughly $116 billion in quarterly sales and projected about $130 billion for the following quarter—staggering numbers that still failed to calm the market.

Inside Nvidia, the transition looked considerably less routine. During the first companywide meeting without Huang, staff had submitted about 700 questions, many concerning compensation and board transparency.

Kress promised pay increases and extra stock awards in December, months earlier than planned. Executives took turns assuring workers that the company could serve customers without Huang; some employees nevertheless discussed leaving if his absence became permanent.

The pushback extended outside headquarters. An online petition gathered roughly 200,000 names, though signers’ claimed employee or shareholder affiliations were not independently verified. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker, whose firms had disclosed about $2.1 billion in Nvidia shares, urged a deliberate succession process that kept Huang’s return possible. It was an unusual message to directors searching for a replacement: don't rush to replace the founder.

This letter was sent to Nvidia's board today.

Absolutely share @altcap belief that this letter outlines minimum acceptable standards. pic.twitter.com/ST2f5TMAa1

— Gavin Baker (@GavinSBaker) November 14, 2026

In other words, Nvidia couldn’t survive the scandal—not the one about Huang cheating, but the one about Huang leaving.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and turned graphics processors into the hardware behind modern AI. But his power also lies in the relationships surrounding those chips: cloud giants buying entire data centers of GPUs, developers locked into Nvidia’s CUDA software, suppliers building its next systems and policymakers deciding which markets it can serve.

Reuters reports that he has overseen roughly 60 direct reports and personally shaped major deals and product decisions.

He has also become a financier and ambassador for the AI ecosystem. Nvidia has invested in companies including CoreWeave and Nebius, which buy computing hardware to rent AI capacity to others.

That web of investment, sales, and financing is precisely why his disappearance unnerved markets far beyond Nvidia. After his outsting, Chinese customers delayed or canceled orders while leadership was unsettled; the whole Nasdaq index and the wider S&P500 crashed and odds for a bubble pop spiked to more than 70% on prediction markets.

Then, on Monday, minutes after his return, CoreWeave and Nebius shares each jumped more than 20% alongside Nvidia which had its best day in history—Huang also probably had his best day ever, too.

To have a grasp of Huang’s influence, one just needs to follow the money.

Elon Musk backed the reinstatement campaign; Y Combinator chief Garry Tan and Epic Games’ Tim Sweeney were among other prominent supporters. Bill Ackman celebrated Monday with “sanity prevails.” Trump pressed the case personally, later saying his intervention was “very important” and that the administration assured directors there was no national security obstacle to Huang’s return.

That backing helps explain the whiplash: On November 17, Jones said the board would not reinstate Huang, citing conduct inconsistent with Nvidia’s standards. Six days later, the same directors voted unanimously to bring him back. They say meetings satisfied them about his candor and leadership, but have not explained exactly what changed. Supporters see recognition of an indispensable founder; critics see a board yielding to powerful outsiders.

Bullish analysts argue that restoring Huang reduces execution and talent-retention risk. Dan Ives has framed Nvidia as a $300 stock with Huang versus $225 without him, while Melius Research upgraded the shares to “buy” with a $220 target.

Yet Monday’s roughly 30%-plus rebound followed a Friday close of $125.53; even near $165, Nvidia remains well below its October peak. Buying the comeback means paying much more for the same projected chip sales.

The other side is harder to price. Michael Burry criticized the reversal, and legal scrutiny of Huang, Nvidia’s export controls and its board continues. The company is establishing a board committee for national security and export-control oversight and recruiting a chief compliance officer.

None of that resolves the fundamental AI question: whether customers can earn enough on massive infrastructure spending to sustain Nvidia’s growth.

Huang’s return repairs a missing link between Nvidia, its customers, Wall Street, and Washington. The 11-day crisis showed how much confidence that link carries—and how vulnerable the AI trade becomes when it breaks.

What he has not yet won back is an unquestioned mandate to lead.

#5016. Bitcoin’s Recovery Faces a New Warning After $2 Billion in ETF Outflows

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Bitcoin recovery above $60,000 is offering some relief after a brutal November sell-off, but the money flowing through US spot Bitcoin ETFs tells a less encouraging story. The funds recorded more than $2 billion in combined net outflows over four consecutive trading sessions ending November 24.

Bitcoin’s return to the psychologically important price level follows a difficult week in which the cryptocurrency traded as low as approximately $55,300.

The rebound is welcome. What is less clear is whether buyers have returned with enough capital to sustain it.

The scale of the recent withdrawals deserves more attention than the recovery itself.

According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $582.3 million on November 19, followed by another $669.2 million the next day. Withdrawals continued on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the combined total across those four trading sessions to approximately $2.05 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for roughly $1.77 billion in net outflows during that period.

Wednesday’s figures are still subject to final reporting confirmation, although available data points to further withdrawals.

These numbers do not mean that every institutional investor is abandoning Bitcoin. ETF shareholders include different types of investors, from financial advisers and asset managers to individual traders. Some may be reducing risk, while others could be unwinding positions that were never intended as long-term investments.

What the figures establish is that the ETF market has experienced persistent net redemptions, even after Bitcoin’s substantial decline.

That is not the response bulls would ideally want to see from buyers following a major correction.

Earlier this week, Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again after an initial recovery above $64,000 failed to hold.

Glassnode’s November 24 report, titled The Canary in the Coal Mine, documented the severity of Bitcoin’s latest decline. The cryptocurrency reached approximately $55,300 on November 21, falling beneath the lows established during the summer.

That matters because investors who bought during previous corrections may now be sitting on losses despite having entered the market at what appeared to be relatively attractive prices.

Glassnode’s historical data reveals another uncomfortable detail. Long-term holders recently accounted for more than 75% of Bitcoin’s realized losses before their share fell back toward 50%. Similar periods of selling at a loss appeared during previous bear markets, although that alone does not establish that Bitcoin has reached a bottom.

Their behavior becomes particularly important when Bitcoin starts recovering.

Some holders may use a rebound to reduce their exposure or exit positions closer to their original purchase price. Others may be willing to hold through further volatility. Which group dominates will influence how much buying is required to sustain the next move higher.

A price that previously attracted buyers can become an area of selling pressure when the market approaches it from below.

This is one reason why reclaiming $60,000 should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation that the correction has ended.

There is a credible argument against interpreting persistent ETF outflows as evidence that Bitcoin must fall further.

Markets can begin recovering before investor sentiment improves. In fact, waiting for every major indicator to turn positive can mean missing a substantial portion of a reversal.

Glassnode’s latest research offers some historical perspective. Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to capital inflows over the preceding year have reached their highest intensity since the FTX collapse in 2022. Previous episodes of heavy losses have occurred near major market bottoms, but severe selling alone is not enough to confirm that a recovery is underway.

Bitcoin also trades across a much broader market than US exchange-traded funds. Direct purchases, overseas exchanges and other investment vehicles can absorb selling even when American funds experience redemptions.

The distinction is between evidence that a market can recover and evidence that it has already established a sustainable recovery.

Bitcoin’s latest bounce demonstrates that buyers are willing to step in at lower prices. It does not yet establish whether those buyers can absorb additional selling at higher levels.

If Bitcoin begins to hold its gains despite persistent ETF withdrawals, that would itself be an encouraging development. It would suggest that demand elsewhere in the market is capable of offsetting some of the pressure coming from the funds.

For now, the price and ETF data leave that question open.

Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday adds another complication to the recovery. US equity markets are closed, removing a regular trading session for American spot Bitcoin ETFs while cryptocurrency exchanges continue operating.

The absence of new ETF flow figures during the holiday should not be confused with an improvement in institutional demand.

With fewer traditional financial market participants active, Bitcoin’s immediate price movements may also provide an incomplete picture of how investors are responding to the recent sell-off.

Friday’s shortened US trading session and the subsequent return to normal market hours will provide more useful evidence.

For traders, the important signals are whether Bitcoin can retain its recent gains, whether ETF redemptions begin to ease and whether buying remains strong enough to absorb selling when normal market participation resumes.

The $60,000 level may dominate the headlines, but the more convincing recovery will be the one that can survive without depending entirely on temporary relief from selling pressure.

#5014. Bitcoin ETFs face record monthly withdrawals – What keeps institutions in?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs faced their worst month since launch, recording approximately $4.94 billion in Net Outflows during November so far. With several days still left, the month had already overtaken June’s $4.51 billion withdrawal.

Yet institutional ownership data offered a different perspective. Billions were leaving the funds, while reported institutional exposure remained substantial.

Just for a quick recap, the year started weak. January recorded $1.61 billion in Net Outflows, followed by $206.52 million in February.

A brief recovery followed. March attracted $1.32 billion in Net Inflows, while April brought another $1.97 billion. May, however, recorded $2.43 billion in Net Outflows. June followed with $4.51 billion, making it the year’s second-worst month.

July’s $172.43 million in Net Inflows offered a near-flat pause before a stronger rebound. August attracted $3.52 billion, followed by $2.65 billion in September. That recovery unravelled in October, when $515.03 million left the funds. November’s $4.94 billion withdrawal then pushed the year towards another low.

In fact, Glassnode also pointed out that Bitcoin ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since launch.

Hence, the persistent selling pressure has raised concerns about institutional confidence in Bitcoin. This is because a closer look at institutional ownership data suggests that Wall Street is not abandoning Bitcoin ETFs just yet.

In fact, institutional participation has continued to expand despite the deteriorating market sentiment, raising an important question: What is keeping institutions invested in Bitcoin ETFs when investors are pulling billions out of them?

According to Bloomberg ETF analyst James Seyffart, 2,223 institutional filers collectively reported approximately $29.77 billion in Bitcoin ETF exposure, equivalent to 356,072 BTC.

Investment advisors accounted for the largest share, with 1,863 filers holding approximately 160,195 BTC worth $13.39 billion. Brokerage firms followed with 59,255 BTC, while hedge funds held approximately 58,088 BTC. Banks and trusts also have considerable exposure, holding 28,937 BTC and 19,723 BTC, respectively.

More importantly, the data shows that institutional ownership increased by 56,493 BTC over the one-year period. Well, according to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions have also added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.

This suggests that the recent outflow streak has not translated into a complete institutional retreat. In this, Wells Fargo has emerged as a major institutional holder, with its aggregated filings showing approximately 30,549 BTC in exposure.

Jane Street, Goldman Sachs, Millennium Management, and Morgan Stanley were also featured among the notable holders. However, the current selling pressure cannot be overlooked.

Ecoinometrics noted that November’s ETF flow trajectory was closely following its bearish simulation. Therefore, if the trend continues, its model suggests Bitcoin could potentially revisit the low-$50,000 range.

#5013. End of Crypto Trading? How AI Replaces Ones Who Pumped Bitcoin (BTC)

The “pump” trade could be taken to new extremes. While some may still be able to use their influence to promote a token, causing others to pile in, it could now be left up to AI to scour socials/wallet activity for abnormal trading volume, assess momentum rankings, etc. and execute on these opportunities faster than those that may be slower to react.

All things considered, agents may exacerbate many of the existing issues with crypto, from short lived moves/reversals, to dangerous herding and even more pronounced drawdowns.

Automation is not necessarily a new occurrence in the space, from simple rule-based trading (implement a certain set of rules when X occurs) to algo trading (use algos to spread out trading activity to avoid market impact), but it appears to be shifting from humans implementing strategies to letting AI make decisions and execute.

A February 2026 study from the Journal of Futures Markets found sub-second trading patterns in BTC/ETH perpetual/spot markets exhibiting behavior consistent with algo trading for liquidity, increasing volatility and trading costs with no significant impact on prices.

In August 2026, Binance rolled out Agent OS allowing builders to access exchange trading functionality and data via AI agents.

Coinbase Ventures released a comprehensive breakdown of the crypto agentic stack from data, to agent building tools, to execution/compliance in November. Instead of dictating each trade, users may be able to assign high-level goals (i.e. follow momentum, hedge position, etc.) for agents to implement 24/7.

Automation will likely accelerate across the crypto space. While macro events, ETF inflows/outflows, large holders, etc. will still have an impact on Bitcoin, it’s likely that many more aspects/trades will become automated.

Time will tell how pervasive agentic trading will become, but the era of a small group of traders/influencers/chat rooms able to move the needle via FOMO/hype seems poised to face stiff competition from AI that never sleeps.

AI is not necessarily intelligent. A 2026 study published in the journal Frontiers in Blockchain studied machine-learning strategies using crypto market data and found that many strategies became highly overfit and offered no viable edge for retail traders once realistic trading fees were taken into account.

Also, strategies that performed well on one cryptocurrency did not necessarily perform well on others. Faster processing speeds can’t make bad data good, can’t identify all false narratives and can’t insulate a strategy from sudden shifts in market regimes.

Are institutional investors still relevant? Can they protect themselves? Absolutely.

Institutions are (and will continue to be) an important source of capital, liquidity and price discovery (particularly for Bitcoin). A 2026 study using BTC data from 2012–2025 found that as the market has matured, Bitcoin has seen increased trading volume, decreasing transaction costs and increasing market efficiency.

Wintermute reported that in the first half of 2026 institutional clients accounted for 72% of total spot trading volume on its OTC desk (note: this is Wintermute’s OTC desk and is not representative of the entire market). It’s also worth noting that many institutional investors do employ quantitative strategies and state-of-the-art execution technologies.

While larger investors may have access to better data, faster infrastructure, cross-venue surveillance capabilities and stricter risk management protocols (and can limit their exposure and monitor abnormal order flow), there’s only so much that institutional investors can do to protect themselves.

Institutional investors can’t control a 24/7 global market with liquidity spread across multiple venues and derivatives markets. They also can’t assume that all AIs are created equal/safe (as Binance’s launch of its own AI demonstrated prompt injection risks and limited visibility into external AIs’ trading logic/reasons for trading).

Finally, during times of stress, risk management/contingency protocols (used by many investors) could be a crowded exit for funds that employ similar strategies.

The future is not “AI replaces every trader.” It will likely see continued automation of certain aspects of trading (i.e. execution, short-term alpha hunting, etc.) and a continued shift in the value-add that humans bring to the table (i.e. capital allocation, risk management, original research, granting/trading bots permission to trade, etc.).

While AI/bots may continue to squeeze spreads in normal market conditions, they may exacerbate drawdowns/cascades during times of market stress as strategies compete with one another.

At the end of the day, Bitcoin will still be bought/sold, it’s just a question of who gets to make those decisions.

#5012. North Korea Moves $247 Million of Binance Hack Loot Through Bitcoin Mixers

North Korea Moves $247 Million of Binance Hack Loot Through Bitcoin Mixers

North Korea’s hackers have now funneled at least $247 million from the record $6.4 billion Binance theft through Bitcoin “coinjoins,” a mixing technique designed to sever the trail between stolen funds and their origin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said.

The figure, roughly a month after the Oct. 29 hack, reflects just the funds pushed into coinjoins, which pool many users’ Bitcoin into a single transaction so the coins can’t be traced.

Notably, almost all of it was coordinated by a single known individual: the operator of Kruw, the most widely used coinjoin coordinator for Wasabi Wallet users. That operator “refuses to block funds such as these,” Elliptic co-founder Tom Robinson told Decrypt in an email, which is why the firm expects the laundering to continue.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The mixing accelerated sharply in mid-November. On Nov. 17, the attacker emptied five of the nine largest Ethereum addresses tied to the theft, shifting about 488,000 ETH ($860 million) into fresh batches.

Those are being steadily swapped into Bitcoin through the Thorchain bridge and then sent into coinjoins, often within hours, the same playbook North Korea used after the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in early 2025.

The operation has spanned more than 27,000 wallets across at least 16 blockchains, roughly 55 services and some 90,000 transactions. Elliptic stressed it is clearly automated but found no evidence AI agents are directing it, pointing instead to conventional software, with fixed timing, set amounts and pauses that resemble human working patterns in Pyongyang.

Elliptic earlier found the hackers even minted their own worthless meme coins to shuffle funds through liquidity pools, one of several obfuscation tactics stacked together alongside cross-chain bridges, asset swaps and lending-vault hops.

The FBI has attributed the theft to the North Korean group TraderTraitor, and Binance has said it will cover all customer losses.

Still, little has actually been cashed out. About $2.85 billion has been frozen, and roughly $2.35 billion remains parked in theft-linked addresses, including the 18,270 BTC taken directly from Binance, which hasn’t moved since the night of the hack.

Elliptic expects the funds to be converted to Bitcoin, mixed and eventually cashed out through over-the-counter brokers over a period of months, the point at which they can still be intercepted.

With the Kruw operator declining to block the flows, though, the mixing shows little sign of slowing.

#5011. Bitwise XRP ETF Averages $14 Million in Daily Trading in Year One

The Bitwise XRP ETF traded an average of about $14 million a day over its first year on the market, resulting in over $3.5 billion in total trading volume, according to Bitwise.

In a post on X commemorating the Bitwise XRP ETF's first anniversary, Bitwise said the fund had recorded over $667 million in net inflows and had more than $376 million in assets under management (AUM) since launch.

Bitwise's XRP ETF started trading on Nov. 20, 2025, on NYSE Arca. It trades under the same ticker as the cryptocurrency it holds, XRP.

Investors can use the ETF's shares to track the price of the token through their brokerage accounts. The fund holds the XRP on behalf of investors. At launch, the ETF charged a 0.34% annual management fee. It also offered a fee waiver for the first $500 million in assets for the first month.

The $3.5 billion in trading volume is the total value of purchases and sales of the ETF's shares. This means the same ETF shares could trade repeatedly. If an investor sells their shares to another investor, that transaction increases trading volume. But the total XRP held in the fund doesn't change in that case.

On the other hand, the $667 million in net inflows represents the total dollar value of new shares issued over the past year minus redeemed shares.

AUM represents the total dollar value of a fund's assets at a specific moment. Since the fund's total assets are valued in dollars, AUM can fall below cumulative net inflows if the price of XRP declines, even as investors continue to put money into the fund.

The quarterly report filed by Bitwise with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) shows the impact of investor demand and XRP's price on the fund over the past year.

The net asset value of the fund increased from $299.1 million at the end of June to $614.9 million at the end of September.

Over $315.7 million was added to the fund's net assets during that quarter. Just over half of that $315.7 million came from new share creations.

The fund issued new shares with a total dollar value of $210.7 million. It also redeemed $32.8 million in shares during that quarter. So that left about $178 million in net new creations.

The fund issued 13.75 million shares and redeemed 2.42 million shares.

#5010. Bitcoin hashrate falls 8% with 11M BTC in loss – 2 reasons bears are watching

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Q4 alone has pushed Bitcoin several years back across multiple market metrics.

Bitcoin’s breakdown to $55k last week took its price back to pre-2024 U.S. elections. So, almost every increase in Bitcoin’s value since the election, even the surge to $126k, has therefore been reversed. The selloff has pushed 11.6 million BTC underwater, the highest on record.

And now, this is starting to affect the Bitcoin options market too.

From the data shown below, BTC options traders are turning increasingly bearish. Put option buying has accelerated to levels last witnessed during BTC’s 2022 capitulation.

Likewise, the put-to-call ratio has reached its highest value since 2021. These extreme readings are rare and suggest that traders are increasingly preparing for more downside.

Naturally, this raises the question: What is driving this shift in sentiment?

From a market psychology perspective, Bitcoin’s [BTC] drop to multi-year lows has put growing pressure on investor profitability. With 11.6 million BTC now underwater, holding through the downturn is becoming a tougher bet, especially in the current macro environment.

Notably, nothing illustrates this better than a recent Glassnode report.

Bitcoin’s falling hashrate has put miner profitability back under pressure.

To date in 2026, MARA Holdings has sold 40,581 BTC at an average price of $74,446, amassing around $3.03 billion. Much of this sale is related to the switch by Bitcoin miners to AI. Yet, the latest figures from Glassnode indicate that there may be further strains on mining.

Bitcoin’s hashrate is currently 8% down on where it was last year, the first time there has been a yearly reduction since China banned mining in 2021. However, whereas the 2021 fall was due to regulatory factors, today’s decline is mainly due to price. The bigger concern is the timing. Just 15 months before the next BTC halving occurs, miners are already contending with reduced profit margins.

In short, Bitcoin’s continued hashrate decline reflects the growing stress across the mining sector.

Miners are already seeing reduced profitability. The upcoming halving will reduce miners’ block reward and so may exacerbate this issue. There is therefore a greater risk that miners may “continue” to switch off hardware and sell Bitcoin to maintain cashflow.

So, for now, the falling hashrate, rising underwater supply, and bearish options positioning all suggest that the market is already preparing for a tougher phase.

Bitcoin’s falling hashrate and tighter mining margins raise fresh fears of miner capitulation.

Bearish options positioning and record-high underwater supply suggest investors are bracing for further downside.
