#5008. Coinbase Reveals COIN Buybacks as It Capitalizes on AI

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that the company is repurchasing stock in the fourth quarter because investors are overlooking the potential of the payments business for AI agents.

"Good to take advantage of market dislocations," said Armstrong.

The company is buying back stock using funds previously authorized for repurchases. He didn't specify the number of COIN shares, the price or the amount spent.

At the start of the quarter, Coinbase had $1.96 billion left to repurchase stock. Over the prior three months, it repurchased 37,995 shares for a total cost of $5.3 million, at an average price of $139.91. All repurchases occurred in August, according to its third-quarter report.

Coinbase's board of directors initially authorized stock buybacks of up to $1 billion in October 2024. A year later, the buyback authorization was doubled. The company also received an option to repurchase some outstanding debt.

The board increased the buyback limit again in January 2026, bringing the total authorization to $4 billion.

Some buybacks have been carried out to cancel stock issued as employee compensation. By the end of September, the company had repurchased 10.2 million Class A shares and canceled more than 85% of the stock issued for employee compensation since the fourth quarter of 2024. This is according to an earnings presentation.

Armstrong envisions a scenario where crypto and AI are involved in different aspects of the same transaction.

For example, AI agents might help users make financial decisions and follow their instructions. Then, a crypto network may be used to transfer funds.

Coinbase wants to provide accounts, payment services, and marketplaces for humans and AI agents to use.

"With AI, everybody has a private banker in your pocket that can help you make better financial decisions," Armstrong posted on Nov. 25.

Coinbase added its wallet and payment services to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments. This offers a way for developers to build agents on Amazon and allow the software to discover paid services. Agents can make small payments when necessary.

Now Armstrong is inviting developers to add their specialized AI models to Agentic.Market.

According to Armstrong, an AI agent can choose which specialist to hire for a task based on its capabilities and price. Coinbase provides the platform where agents can find specialists and pay them.

#5007. CleanSpark is selling Bitcoin to fund its AI expansion as annual losses approach $1 billion

The miner is turning to its Bitcoin treasury to finance acquisitions without diluting shareholders as mining profitability deteriorates.

CleanSpark has begun selling Bitcoin from its treasury to finance acquisitions as the company accelerates its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure.

During the company's Nov. 24 earnings call, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark had sold some of its Bitcoin holdings since the end of September to strengthen its cash position ahead of anticipated acquisitions.

“We've sold some Bitcoin to pad the balance sheet with cash to prepare for some acquisitions that we expect to make in the near future.”

Vecchiarelli added that CleanSpark could sell additional Bitcoin or borrow against its holdings to finance acquisitions without diluting existing shareholders. The company also intends to sell virtually all newly mined Bitcoin to fund daily operations.

CleanSpark ended September with approximately $1.3 billion in reported liquidity, comprising $204.8 million in cash and cash equivalents and approximately $1.13 billion in Bitcoin holdings and related exposure.

The company reported exposure equivalent to 13,530 BTC at fiscal year-end but has not disclosed how much Bitcoin it subsequently sold.

The treasury strategy comes as deteriorating Bitcoin mining economics weigh on CleanSpark's financial performance.

According to its fiscal 2026 results, annual revenue declined 25% to $576.5 million, while the company recorded a net loss of $987.1 million, compared with net income of $364 million a year earlier.

Vecchiarelli attributed approximately two-thirds of the earnings reversal to noncash adjustments in the value of its Bitcoin holdings.

However, profitability also deteriorated across its mining operations. Annual gross margins contracted from 55% to 41% as the average value of mined Bitcoin fell from approximately $97,600 to $79,500.

The decline occurred despite improvements in fleet efficiency and a reduction in electricity costs from $0.057 to $0.055 per kilowatt-hour.

Against this backdrop, CleanSpark is directing more capital toward AI data centers and acquiring land and power infrastructure.

The company secured a 20-year, $6.6 billion lease with an investment-grade tenant at its Sandersville facility in Georgia and raised $2.276 billion through secured notes to fully fund the project's development. It also expanded its Texas infrastructure portfolio through acquisitions supporting up to 885 MW of power capacity.

Vecchiarelli said management sees further acquisition opportunities as a better use of available capital than repurchasing CleanSpark shares, despite believing its stock is undervalued.

While Bitcoin provides CleanSpark with an alternative to equity financing, the cryptocurrency's recent decline has reduced the collateral value supporting its existing borrowing.

CleanSpark's annual filing showed that it had borrowed $90 million through a $100 million revolving credit facility with Two Prime Lending as of Sept. 30.

The company pledged 1,665 BTC worth $139.1 million at the time, giving the loan a loan-to-value ratio of approximately 65%.

Under the agreement, a ratio exceeding 74% triggers a margin call, while liquidation can occur above 80%. Based on the September loan balance and collateral, those thresholds correspond to Bitcoin prices of approximately $73,046 and $67,568, respectively.

With Bitcoin trading near $59,000 on Nov. 25, the same collateral would be worth approximately $98.2 million, pushing the loan-to-value ratio to nearly 92% if the position remained unchanged.

#5006. COLDCARD bug goes undetected for 5 years despite 15 security reviews: Details

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Coinkite, the company behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.

According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the issue affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.

Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.

That said, the issue stemmed from a software integration error that caused certain Coldcard devices to use a weaker pseudo-random number generator instead of the intended hardware-based system.

This generator produced less unpredictable recovery phrases, making it easier for attackers to guess the private keys and access users’ Bitcoin. Although the recovery phrases appeared normal and passed some security tests, they did not offer the expected level of protection.

As a result, the vulnerability reportedly resulted in the theft of at least 1,789 BTC, worth approximately $114.7 million at the time. As of 18th November, Coinkite had received around 300 loss-related support tickets linked to 242 customer accounts. However, the actual number of victims could be higher.

That said, vulnerability significantly reduced the difficulty of reconstructing affected wallet seeds. According to Coinkite, the affected seeds had approximately 40 bits of effective entropy on Mk2 and Mk3 devices and 72 bits on Mk4, Mk5, and Q devices.

This was considerably weaker than the originally intended 128-bit security. This allowed attackers to use offline brute-force searches to reconstruct private keys and gain access to Bitcoin holdings without physically accessing the hardware wallets.

However, Coinkite did address the issue on 31st July and introduced additional security measures in August. Yet, it is still investigating the incident alongside law enforcement authorities and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

Up until now, the company has not finalized a compensation plan. Regardless, it has been advised that the affected users must generate entirely new recovery phrases and transfer their Bitcoin to new wallets.

This is because simply updating the firmware will not secure previously compromised recovery phrases.

All of this coincided with Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warning that artificial intelligence could potentially discover mathematical shortcuts to break the cryptographic systems protecting crypto private keys.

At the same time, crypto security losses surged 55% to $1.18 billion in Q3 2026, up from $763.97 million in Q2, while reported breaches increased from 67 to 107.

In that, compromised suppliers, delayed patches, and unaudited components accounted for 77% of losses, highlighting risks beyond smart contract vulnerabilities. Lastly, smart contract flaws also caused $569.5 million in losses, while access control and operational failures contributed to another $477.6 million.

#5005. XRP Ledger Bug That Makes Trading Orders Disappear Is Addressed

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Official XRP Ledger's repository account received a proposed fix to keep only transaction-independent offer removals after a tec that should address the disappearance of failed transactions.

This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back. In some circumstances, offers can be removed when a "tec" failure occurs, even though the transaction that triggered it never succeeded.

In one scenario, a trader could have an existing offer removed before they’re able to add a replacement (for instance, if they don’t have enough reserve to add a new offer). In another, a more complicated Flow could temporarily leave an offer unfunded, only to have funds restored if a subsequent step fails, again resulting in an offer being removed even though the transaction that triggered it failed.

To address this issue, rippled will attempt to remove offers that were marked for removal upon tec failure any time a tec failure occurs. Previously, this was attempted for certain tec error codes but not others, with some additional restrictions around Flow-related offer removals (an offer will only be marked for removal if the owner’s balance has not changed in any relevant ways during the course of the Flow).

Offers that have already expired can still be removed, but offers owned by the transactor will be skipped. This is a best effort to make sure offers are consistently added/removed from the order book and should reduce confusing trade results.

Offers to/from regular XRP accounts and balances, XRP sends are unaffected and there are no proposed API changes.

This does not change XRP supply, fees, transaction capacity, etc. and is unlikely to have any effect on XRPL usage or XRP price (other than maybe making XRPL trading more appealing to traders).

This change would mostly affect traders using decentralized exchanges (DEXs) and particularly those using complex/routed/fill-or-kill orders/self-crosses.

On November 23, XRP briefly hit $1.026 before dropping below $1. Reports indicate crypto selling in general and ETF outflows have been putting pressure on XRP lately. By November 25, XRP was trading at ~$0.92. This software change would not be a catalyst for a price recovery of XRP.

#5004. Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use

Compare the top hardware and software crypto wallets to find your safest, easiest self-custody setup.

Keeping your cryptocurrency on an exchange is convenient, but it comes with risks. If the exchange gets hacked, freezes withdrawals, or runs into financial trouble, accessing your funds can become difficult. Using a self-custody wallet gives you direct control over your private keys and, ultimately, your crypto.

Whether you are holding Bitcoin for the next decade, trading memecoins on Solana, or exploring decentralized finance (DeFi), choosing the right wallet matters. Some wallets are designed to keep your assets as secure as possible, while others make it easier to trade, manage tokens, and connect to Web3 apps.

To help you find the right option, we’ve put together a list of seven popular crypto wallets, covering what each one does best, its main advantages, and what to consider before choosing it.

*Prices change frequently, so always confirm on the manufacturer’s official website.

If your primary goal is long-term wealth preservation, Ledger remains the industry benchmark for cold storage.

Unlike mobile apps that stay connected to the internet, Ledger devices store your private keys inside an offline, certified Secure Element chip, the same class of chip used in passports and credit cards (check Ledger’s website for the current certification details).

Through the Ledger Live companion app, you can buy, swap, and stake thousands of coins and tokens. Your private keys never leave the device. Ledger Live runs on your connected phone or computer, but transactions are signed on the Ledger itself.

For those who live by the motto “don’t trust, verify,” Trezor is the gold standard. Contrary to the competitors that keep parts of their code proprietary, Trezor’s firmware is fully open-source, meaning independent security researchers constantly audit it for vulnerabilities.

The Trezor Safe 5 pairs this transparency with a vibrant color touchscreen, haptic feedback, and an EAL6+ Secure Element. It also offers a dedicated Bitcoin-only firmware option for maximalists who want to minimize attack surfaces.

When it comes to interacting with decentralized applications (DApps), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and NFT marketplaces, MetaMask is the undisputed gateway to Web3.

Available as both a browser extension and a mobile app, MetasMask connects seamlessly to virtually every Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) network, including Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base, and BNB Chain.

Modern updates have expanded MetaMask beyond Ethereum via MetaMask Snaps and allow users to add support for non-EVM ecosystems like Bitcoin and Solana directly inside the same interface.

Originally built as the flagship wallet for the Solana ecosystem, Phantom has evolved into one of the fastest, cleanest multi-chain wallets on the market. Today, it seamlessly supports Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Bitcoin in a single unified interface.

What sets Phantom apart is user experience. Transaction simulations show you exact balance changes before you hit approve, and its automated spam filter hides malicious airdrop NFTs so beginners don’t accidentally click phishing links.

If you want one smartphone app that holds virtually every cryptocurrency in existence without manual network configuration, Trust Wallet is built for you.

Supporting over 100 blockchains and millions of digital assets, it removes the technical friction of adding custom RPC networks or hunting down token contract addresses.

It also includes a built-in Web3 browser, straightforward in-app staking for major proof-of-stake coins, and an integrated Security Scanner that flags risky smart contracts.

Many newcomers confuse the main Coinbase exchange app with Coinbase Wallet, but they are completely separate products. Coinbase Wallet is a true non-custodial wallet—meaning you hold your own 12-word recovery phrase, and Coinbase cannot freeze or access your funds.

Note that the app’s branding has changed recently: Coinbase renamed it “Base App” in July 2025 and restored the Coinbase Wallet name in September 2026. It has since shifted toward multichain trading, including perpetual futures, prediction markets, and tokenized stocks, so some of its features are now aimed at more active traders.

Its biggest advantage is frictionless onboarding. You can link your exchange account to transfer funds into self-custody in seconds, claim a free human-readable username instead of copying long hexadecimal addresses, and explore Base and Ethereum DApps.

Traditional hardware wallets require cables, batteries, and carefully guarding a 24-word paper backup. Tangem reimagines cold storage as a sleek, waterproof smart card—roughly the size and thickness of a standard bank debit card.

To approve a transaction, you simply tap the card against the back of your NFC-enabled smartphone. Tangem comes in sets of two or three cards that act as physical backups for one another, allowing you to skip vulnerable paper seed phrases entirely (though a traditional seed option is still available if you prefer it).

Understanding the difference between hot and cold storage saves you from overpaying—or worse, leaving your funds exposed:

A common rule of thumb among experienced crypto investors is to use both, for example keeping around 90% of long-term holdings in a cold wallet and about 10% in a hot wallet for everyday trading and Web3 exploration. This is a guideline, not a standard – adjust it to your own situation.

With crypto, there’s no bank to call if something goes wrong. Transactions are usually irreversible, and if an exchange freezes withdrawals or goes bankrupt, your funds could be stuck for months or even years.

That’s why choosing the best crypto wallet matters. It gives you more control over your money and lets you manage your funds without relying on an exchange.

Your cryptocurrency is not stored inside the physical device—it lives on the blockchain. If your Ledger, Trezor, or Tangem card is lost, stolen, or broken, you can buy a replacement device and restore full access to your funds in minutes using your 12- or 24-word recovery phrase (or backup Tangem card).

While no system is 100% immune, cold hardware wallets cannot be hacked remotely because your private keys stay offline. Most wallet “hacks” happen when users accidentally sign a malicious smart contract on a phishing website or store their seed phrase digitally where malware can find it.

Software wallets like MetaMask, Phantom, and Trust Wallet are completely free to download and hold crypto in. Hardware wallets require an upfront purchase (typically $55 to $250). Regardless of the wallet you choose, you will still pay standard blockchain network (“gas”) fees whenever you send or swap tokens.

With a custodial wallet (like a standard exchange account), a third-party company holds your private keys and can freeze or restrict your withdrawals. With a non-custodial (self-custody) wallet, only you hold the private keys—meaning nobody can block your transactions, though you are solely responsible for backing up your recovery phrase.

No. Unlike traditional bank accounts, funds in a self-custody crypto wallet are not covered by government deposit insurance like the FDIC or SIPC. Because you act as your own bank, protecting your recovery phrase and verifying transaction details before approving them is your primary safeguard.

#5002. Ripple’s latest banking partnership opens another route to XRP adoption in Turkey

Yapı Kredi is building its own crypto trading platform, while existing Ripple partner Garanti BBVA already supports XRP trading and withdrawals.

Ripple has partnered with Turkish banking giant Yapı Kredi to provide digital asset custody infrastructure for its cryptocurrency business.

In a Nov. 25 statement, Yapı Kredi said it has deployed Ripple Custody within its own infrastructure to safeguard digital assets held through Yapı Kredi Kripto, its cryptocurrency trading platform.

The partnership expands Ripple's presence in Türkiye, where financial institutions are increasingly developing regulated digital asset services.

Yapı Kredi is one of the country's largest private banks, with total assets of 4.4 trillion Turkish lira as of September. The lender operates 723 branches nationwide and employs more than 14,000 people.

The bank already facilitates round-the-clock lira transfers between its customers' bank accounts and cryptocurrency exchanges BtcTurk and Paribu.

Ripple disclosed an on-site custody deployment at Yapı Kredi. Garanti BBVA Kripto publishes active XRP trading and withdrawal statuses.

Customers need a lira funding route, an XRP buy option and a way to move XRP off the platform.

Garanti’s lira instruction covers account activation. Its public withdrawal status omits the network. The diagram compares published service details as of Nov. 25.

Compare public bank and platform materials checked on Nov. 25, 2026. Filled points show published features or status. The separate activation point identifies a bank-transfer step whose documented purpose is account activation. Hollow points mark unconfirmed retail steps.

Garanti’s lira instruction covers account activation. Its public withdrawal status omits the network. The diagram compares published service details as of Nov. 25.

However, Yapı Kredi has been developing infrastructure to offer cryptocurrency services through its own subsidiary.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

In October, Yapı Kredi Kripto selected financial technology provider Integral to support digital asset trading, complementing the custody infrastructure it has now secured through Ripple.

Eylem Karaca, an executive at Yapı Kredi Technology, said:

“As digital assets become an increasingly important part of the financial ecosystem, we're focused on building the secure, reliable infrastructure needed to support this evolution.”

The partnership comes as Türkiye's regulatory framework creates commercial opportunities for institutional cryptocurrency custody providers.

Under rules introduced by the country's Capital Markets Board, cryptocurrency trading platforms must hold at least 95% of customer digital assets with authorized custodians.

Ripple said it is the only custody technology provider working with Türkiye's major licensed bank-based crypto custodians, positioning the company to benefit from traditional financial institutions entering the market.

Türkiye ranks among the world's ten largest retail cryptocurrency markets, according to TRM Labs, with demand supported by persistent lira depreciation and interest in alternative savings instruments.

Ripple also identified XRP as one of the country's most widely held digital assets.

The company previously partnered with Garanti BBVA Kripto and IBM in October 2024 to strengthen the custody infrastructure supporting the bank-backed cryptocurrency platform.

Garanti BBVA Kripto served more than 14,000 users at the time and offered services involving Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and several other digital assets.

The platform now supports direct XRP trading against the Turkish lira, alongside XRP deposits and withdrawals.

Yapı Kredi has yet to disclose its retail launch date or the cryptocurrencies it supports. A similar offering would give Turkish investors another bank-backed channel to buy and hold XRP.

#5001. Dogecoin Creator Explains Why No One Can Predict Crypto Prices

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Dogecoin co-founder Billy Markus, who is known on X as Shibetoshi Nakamoto, has explained why, in his opinion, no one can predict the prices of cryptocurrencies.

Markus shared his opinion on Wednesday in a reply to an X post with a prediction that the price of Zcash (ZEC) would fall to $100.

"my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except that people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind," the Dogecoin co-founder wrote.

Markus did not mention Zcash or any other token by name in his reply, and his post was about every single cryptocurrency on the market, including the one he created himself.

my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind

At the time of the post, ZEC was trading at around $728, up by 41.3% over the past year, according to price data on X.

The latest comment from Markus comes a week after Bitwise filed an S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash ETF. According to the filing, the fund is set to trade on the Texas Stock Exchange under the ticker ZEC, and it will not stake ZEC or use shielded transactions.

Markus created Dogecoin together with Jackson Palmer in December 2013. The two developers based the cryptocurrency on the Doge meme with a Shiba Inu dog, and they launched it as a joke about the crypto market of that time.

Markus has said in the past that it took him a couple of hours to write the code of Dogecoin. In 2021, Markus also said on X that he had sold all of his DOGE in 2015 after he lost his job, and that he got about the price of a used Honda Civic for it.

Since then, Markus has stayed active on X under the Shibetoshi Nakamoto name, and he often replies to posts about crypto prices, forecasts and new tokens.

In June 2022, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates spoke about crypto and NFTs at the TechCrunch Sessions: Climate conference.

"As an asset class, it's 100% based on the greater fool theory — that somebody's going to pay more for it than I do," Gates said.

Earlier, at the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting in April 2022, Warren Buffett said that he would not buy all of the Bitcoin in the world even for $25.

"If you told me you own all of the bitcoin in the world and you offered it to me for $25, I wouldn't take it because what would I do with it?" Buffett said.

According to Buffett, Bitcoin does not produce anything. At the same meeting, Buffett compared it with farmland and apartment buildings, and he said that he would pay for a share of them because farmland produces food and apartments produce rent.

#5000. Why One Math Proof Has AI Experts Warning Humans Might Soon Lose Control

Why One Math Proof Has AI Experts Warning Humans Might Soon Lose Control

Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang warned Sunday that artificial superintelligence is approaching—and that humanity may be unable to control systems far smarter than itself.

In an essay on X titled “Superintelligence is Arriving,” Wang said the next year could determine how people live alongside machines capable of improving themselves. His catalyst was an extraordinary mathematics result involving Anthropic’s Claude.

“Superintelligence is arriving. How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in,” Wang wrote.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Wang called the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis a greater intellectual achievement than building the atomic bomb, which he described as a “homework problem” by comparison. The breakthrough, he wrote, came with help from an “alien mind that we don’t understand.”

The warning carries extra weight because Wang runs Meta Superintelligence Labs. Mark Zuckerberg brought him aboard in 2025 after Meta invested $14.3 billion for a 49% stake in Wang’s startup, Scale AI.

On Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he and Claude had proved the Riemann Hypothesis, a conjecture about prime numbers that had resisted mathematicians since 1859. The claim arrived a day after Anthropic’s massive IPO.

Alpöge released roughly 17 million lines of code in Lean, a system that checks mathematical proofs. On Saturday, the Lean and Mathlib communities certified that the code proves the correct statement; researchers are still working to explain its mathematics in conventional form.

For Wang, the result suggests raw reasoning power is no longer AI’s central limitation. He argued that the remaining hurdles involve specialist knowledge, experimentation, and the tools needed to apply intelligence in other fields.

That includes AI research itself. If machines can redesign more capable successors, Wang fears a cycle of recursive self-improvement could move faster than human monitoring or intervention.

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” he wrote. He also questioned human control over hypothetical systems “1000x smarter” than people.

Wang criticized the industry’s “lazy thinking” that superintelligence is inevitable and the only question is making it safe. “We should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI,” he wrote, advocating technology that strengthens human decision-making.

In a Monday follow-up, he said Meta had delayed its Muse launch for months over safety concerns and backed industry safeguards. Zuckerberg, he added, wants most computing power devoted to serving customers rather than unrestricted self-improvement.

Meta nevertheless has its own ambitions. Its Muse Wonder models, released in October, compete with systems from OpenAI and Anthropic, making Wang both a critic of the race’s direction and a leading participant.

Not everyone accepts his leap from mathematics to superintelligence. NYU professor Andrew Gordon Wilson argued that proving an existing conjecture is different from inventing new mathematical frameworks such as calculus or relativity.

“Nothing compares to proving the Riemann Hypothesis in terms of sheer intellectual might”. I disagree. The introduction of calculus, general relativity, and quantum mechanics, are more profound intellectual achievements. Creativity, taste, and intuition is the difference.

— Andrew Gordon Wilson (@andrewgwils) November 23, 2026

The Riemann result demonstrates a remarkable human-AI collaboration, but it does not prove that autonomous superintelligence exists.

Wang has urged the industry to change course while Meta continues developing the systems he fears could eventually exceed human oversight.

Bitcoin's long-term trend value, based on various models like "Plan B", has been set ridiculously high, so chasing targets set by those models might not be the best decision out there, considering modern market conditions.

A revised Bitcoin Power Law model sets BTC's long-term price at $99,000, which is almost $50,000 below the $146,725 estimate that has been used by the traditional Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model.

The creator of the newer, accordingly more accurate model believes the Bitcoin Power Law is still valid, but the fair value is certainly nowhere near the relevant market conditions.

One way or another, the newer models still set the current price threshold at one of the lowest historical levels in the history of the asset—approximately the 1st percentile of its distribution, which means that it stands among 60 of Bitcoin's daily closes that fell below this threshold.

The new model uses a completely different method for calculation: Quantile Regression instead of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). The main difference is that OLS guesses Bitcoin's price trend based on its historical averages, while QR uses specific points in the price distribution, not an average. Essentially, the newer calculation model smoothens out extremes that made OLS less accurate.

Despite the newer calculation and estimation approach, the improved calculation algorithm and everything else, models are estimating, not making solid predictions.

There are thousands of other factors to consider when determining Bitcoin's next move, so any kind of model is useful only for evaluating the momentum and historical significance of the most recent movements.

The model also places its 0.1 percentile at $55,185, a level below which Bitcoin has closed only six times. The creator argues that only the lower part of Bitcoin's price distribution, between the 0.1 and 5th percentiles, may continue following the Power Law, while higher levels gradually move down towards this lower boundary.

The model also uses Protocol Time instead of Calendar Time. Still, its creator maintains that the Power Law is not broken. The problem, according to this view, is how previous models measured it and how much they allowed market bubbles to influence the results.

#4997. Bitcoin Falls as PCE Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Falls as PCE Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected

Heavy ETF outflows, surging put bets, and fragile support leave traders watching whether a deeper slide is just beginning.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Wednesday, trading at around $58,220 as concerns about further losses grew ahead of Thanksgiving. The BTC price dropped 2.8% in 24 hours following the release of October inflation data, which showed that price pressures remained elevated according to the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure.

The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% in October, matching September’s increase.

Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed 0.3% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier. Headline PCE inflation increased 3.8% from a year earlier.

The report also showed that US personal income rose 0.7% in October, while consumer spending increased 0.3%. However, real consumer spending was virtually unchanged, suggesting that higher prices continued to weigh on purchasing power.

Bitcoin price fell to about $55,300 over the weekend before recovering to around $64,400 on Tuesday on renewed stock market optimism after Nvidia reinstated its CEO, Jensen Huang.

However, the major crypto “acted as the canary in the coal mine”, according to Glassnode: BTC fully gave back the NVIDIA-driven rally within hours while stocks lagged, then came under pressure. Price broke the $62,000–66,000 support zone, retested summer lows, and is struggling to hold around the $60,000 level.

Bitcoin lost nearly 26% of its value over the past 30 days, and the realized losses are the heaviest since the FTX crash in November 2022.

In addition to that, approximately 90% of the tracked leveraged long positions between the previous week’s market price and Bitcoin’s realized price ($53,200) have been liquidated.

Glassnode suggests that much of the selling pressure is coming from the US. Over the past 20 trading days, US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen around $4.3 billion in net outflows, marking one of their biggest periods of withdrawals since launch.

Spot market activity tells a similar story: over the past 30 days, US investors on Coinbase have been net sellers, while buying and selling on Binance have remained relatively balanced.

Glassnode’s latest data shows growing bearishness among Bitcoin options traders, with limited support against sharp price movements around current levels. Between $58K and $64K, options dealers are positioned in a way that could amplify volatility, potentially accelerating a sell-off if prices fall further.

Meanwhile, bearish bets are rising. Traders bought 1.7 put options for every call last week, the highest ratio since June 2022. Similar levels of pessimism appeared near Bitcoin’s 2022 market low, although prices continued falling for several more months.

Glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s current decline may not be over. Bitcoin price remains weaker than traditional equities, US buying demand is lacking, and the market is struggling to hold its summer lows.

Glassnode identifies $60,000 as a key level to watch. A decisive break below it, followed by a close under $58,500, could open the door to a decline towards $53,200.

A recovery above $60,000, supported by renewed spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, would offer stronger evidence that the market is stabilising.

#4996. UK to test whether AI can replace a second mammogram reader in trial of 660,000 women

A UK trial aiming to enroll 660,000 women will assess AI’s impact on breast cancer detection, recalls, and NHS workload.

Women in Cambridgeshire are the first to join a UK trial testing whether AI can take on the second check of a screening mammogram.

The study will compare two AI approaches with the usual two-reader process, and researchers will measure how many cancers each approach detects and how often women are called back for further tests.

NIHR Cambridge reported the first enrollments on Nov. 23. The study, known as EDITH, aims to enroll 660,000 women across about 30 UK breast screening centers, according to the ISRCTN trial registry.

Eligible women receive information about the trial and how to opt out with their screening invitation. The appointment itself proceeds as usual, and every mammogram in the trial still gets at least one human read.

EDITH randomly assigns clinic days to one of three approaches, and each participating center uses all three. Under standard screening, two NHS experts read the images. In one trial arm, an expert reads the mammogram first, then AI checks for signs of cancer the expert may have missed.

In the other AI arm, the software assesses the images first, and one NHS expert reads mammograms the tool rates as low likelihood for cancer, and two read those it rates as high likelihood.

A very high score or a disagreement about whether to call a woman back sends the case for an additional human review. Across all three groups, at least two human experts make final decisions about cancer detection.

Researchers will compare each AI approach separately with standard double reading.

The registered study design treats at least one additional cancer detected per 1,000 women screened as a meaningful gain. For recalls, it sets a comparison margin of up to two extra callbacks per 1,000 women screened relative to standard double reading.

Both rates are calculated across all women screened.

The two rates capture different steps in screening, and staff counts a callback when they ask a woman to return for more tests. The cancer detection rate counts cancers found during the screening episode.

Researchers will count how many readings staff carry out, how many cases need an extra expert review, and how many women are called back for assessment. The study will also track cancers found between screening rounds.

NIHR Cambridge says the NHS would change routine screening only if the evidence shows the new approach is as safe and effective as the care women receive today.

#4995. Ripple Custody Partners With Major Private Bank in Türkiye

Ripple has once again landed a major partnership in Türkiye, but this time around with one of the country’s largest private banks, putting XRP in the spotlight.

While this comes as part of Ripple’s growing expansion into the traditional financial space, the blockchain firm announced it has partnered with Yapı Kredi, a major Turkish private bank, to support its cryptocurrency business.

As part of the partnership agreement, Ripple Custody will help the bank to securely manage its digital assets and provide custody services for its crypto trading platform dubbed Yapı Kredi Kripto.

While the partnership demands the full integration of the Ripple custodial infrastructure, the firm revealed that Ripple Custody will be installed on the bank's own premises.

This way, Yapı Kredi will have access to adequate security and control it needs to manage all digital assets on behalf of its customers, boosting its security.

The development is significant for the bank and the broader Turkish crypto market; it also marks a major milestone for Ripple as the firm claims to be the only custody service provider currently supporting leading Turkish banks licensed by the CMB as crypto asset custodians.

It is important to note that Türkiye currently stands as one of the world's top 10 retail crypto markets, with XRP recorded as one of its most widely used cryptocurrencies.

With Yapı Kredi now fortifying its position as a major player in Türkiye’s fast-growing crypto market, its partnership with the blockchain firm associated with XRP is likely to open new opportunities for XRP while positioning it for bigger adoption in the country.

#4993. OpenAI Will Pay You Up to $8K to Preach the AI Gospel to Small Businesses

OpenAI Will Pay You Up to $8K to Preach the AI Gospel to Small Businesses

OpenAI wants people to spread the gospel of ChatGPT to their local businesses. And it is willing to pay them up to $8,000 a month to do it.

The company launched OpenWorks, a program that recruits AI-savvy individuals and small consulting teams to help neighborhood businesses figure out what to do with the technology. The idea is to move beyond telling a restaurant owner that AI will change everything and actually build something useful for the restaurant.

OpenAI will pay selected partners a monthly stipend of up to $8,000. In exchange, applicants must commit to four full days of free, in-person work with local businesses each month, plus one community workshop. It's not an $8,000 salary just for being good at prompts.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

That said, this isn't a full-time job with an automatic $96,000 salary. The company advertises a maximum monthly stipend and asks partners to spend four full days each month providing free, in-person assistance, plus hosting one community workshop.

The application asks candidates to describe a real problem they've solved using AI, what changed afterward, and which businesses they'd help first. Knowing how to give ChatGPT clever instructions apparently isn't enough; experience in coding, automation, marketing or operations helps.

Small businesses pay nothing for the service. They pick a problem, work with a partner on a solution, and get three months of ChatGPT Business at no cost. OpenAI says the pilot covers independently owned U.S. businesses, but leaves out startups backed by venture capital, private-equity-owned companies, and software firms.

The company has some examples to sell the idea. In Fargo, North Dakota, the owners of Tiny Things, a gift shop selling miniatures, used ChatGPT with an OpenWorks partner to build an inventory dashboard. One owner estimated that commissioning a similar tool would have cost about $50,000.

In Charleston, a microgreens grower used the chatbot to find restaurants and write personalized pitches to chefs. He estimates his response rate went from 20% to 75% and says he landed 10 new restaurant customers in four months. Those are the businesses' own accounts, not independently audited results.

OpenWorks is starting in 20 communities, including New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Fargo. OpenAI is inviting applicants elsewhere, too, under the slogan "Help us reach every community in America."

The push comes as the company works to turn consumer enthusiasm into recurring business usage. As Decrypt reported in April, enterprise customers already accounted for more than 40% of OpenAI's revenue, according to the company.

Competition also provides an incentive. Anthropic overtook OpenAI in one measure of business AI adoption earlier this year, even as ChatGPT remained a major consumer destination.

Getting ChatGPT into more neighborhood businesses gives OpenAI another route to paying customers, though the company hasn't said what happens after the free three-month offer. It also follows an October effort with America's Small Business Development Centers to train advisers and reach at least 1,000 businesses through workshops.

OpenAI has not announced a general application deadline or a fixed stipend for everyone accepted. The form is open now, and its most important question is pretty straightforward: Can you actually show up four full days a month and help somebody run a business better?

#4991. NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role

Home » Trendsetter News » NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role

NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.

The New York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.

Her distinction: settling share ownership and moving money across currencies are separate jobs, and winning one does not automatically secure the other.

According to Dr. Stevenson, Ava Labs announced that Avalanche would provide the core ledger for the clearing firm behind the proposed platform.

She cites Wall Street Journal reporting that Avalanche would be its sole settlement blockchain, with regulatory approval still required.

The proposed venue would support around-the-clock trading and near-instant settlement. Stevenson says NYSE tested Avalanche for roughly a year, prioritizing transaction speed, predictable costs and control over who can participate.

That permissioning capability matters for a regulated exchange. Avalanche (AVAX) can support customized networks with participation restrictions, rather than requiring the exchange to conduct settlement on an unrestricted public network.

AVAX rose as much as roughly 10% on the news, according to the video. Stevenson, who discloses holding the token, calls the selection a win for Avalanche, but cautions against treating infrastructure adoption as proof of investment returns.

“A network being used by a big name and its token being needed” are different things, she says. The announcement, in her account, provided neither revenue figures nor a commitment that NYSE would buy or hold AVAX.

Dr. Stevenson’s XRP thesis centers on overseas investors funding dollar-denominated stock purchases outside conventional banking hours.

A trader holding yen or another currency would need access to dollars or dollar-linked funding before buying U.S. shares.

She argues that this creates an opportunity for cross-border payment infrastructure, including XRP. But it remains a proposed use case, not a disclosed partnership: “I’m not telling you that NYSE is going to pick XRP for that.”

The YouTube video episode does not establish that XRP would be necessary for such funding. Nor does expanded trading access, by itself, demonstrate future demand for the token.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson also says the platform would support tokenized stocks issued across multiple blockchains, distinguishing asset issuance from the ledger used for settlement.

Those details matter more than a simple Avalanche-versus-XRP contest: the unresolved questions are which services institutions actually adopt, what generates revenue, and whether that activity requires either token.

#4990. Bitcoin ETFs shed $4 billion — How did one fund hide the cracks before leading the exit?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $4.14 billion over three weeks, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly 84% of the withdrawals. However, the same fund had been concealing weakness elsewhere just weeks ago. The story behind the numbers is considerably more complicated than the headline.

In the week leading up to October 19, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs appeared to be doing rather well. The funds collectively attracted $301.2 million in net inflows. That’s quite a reassuring development for a market that had become accustomed to treating ETF demand as a barometer of Bitcoin’s institutional appeal.

There was one small complication, though. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) had brought in $565.7 million on its own. Every other fund combined lost $264.5 million. So, how healthy was that $301.2 million gain if it depended entirely on one fund?

Three weeks later, the answer became harder to ignore.

Between November 2 and 20, Bitcoin ETFs suffered a staggering $4.14 billion in net withdrawals, according to Farside Investors. By the way, IBIT ALONE accounted for approximately $3.49 billion, or 84% of the exodus.

And the selling gathered pace as the week wore on. Nearly $1.79 billion left in the final week, around 1.7 times the previous week’s withdrawals. From November 17 through November 20, each trading session ended with a larger outflow than the previous one.

October’s biggest source of support had become November’s biggest source of pressure. The reversal was striking enough. In fact, what was happening beneath it was more revealing!

BlackRock’s influence on the industry’s performance was hardly a one-week curiosity.

The pattern continued into October 26–30. IBIT attracted another $176.9 million while competing funds collectively lost $379.3 million. Even though the industry finished that week in the red, BlackRock’s inflows effectively absorbed nearly half the damage.

Spot BTC ETFs recorded roughly $643 million in withdrawals in a single session, with IBIT contributing approximately $234 million. The fund that had been cushioning the industry’s losses was now participating in them.

November made that reversal unmistakable.

IBIT accounted for approximately 94% of the industry’s net outflows during the first week, 85% during the second, and 76% during the third. Curiously, its share declined even as the third week brought the industry’s biggest outflow yet.

That was the more consequential development. Other funds, including Fidelity’s FBTC and products from Grayscale and ARK, were contributing increasingly to the selling. What had initially been concentrated overwhelmingly in BlackRock’s product was beginning to spread.

A market once held up by its largest fund was now being dragged down by it, with competitors increasingly joining the retreat.

Now, IBIT was already by far the industry’s biggest fund. Perhaps its dominance in the withdrawals was simply a consequence of its size. Hence why that possibility deserved a closer look. However, a closer look at this position revealed another complication.

A fund holding most of the industry’s assets will naturally account for a significant share of its movements. A billion dollars leaving a $60 billion product is hardly equivalent to the same amount leaving one worth $5 billion.

By October 30, IBIT held approximately $62.7 billion in Bitcoin, according to iShares holdings data. Looking at it broadly, the Bitcoin ETF market held roughly $98.14 billion, based on SoSoValue.

BlackRock therefore controlled about two-thirds of the industry’s assets entering November. And yet, it accounted for 84% of the subsequent three-week net withdrawals.

The disparity only becomes sharper when adjusted for size.

IBIT’s $3.49 billion outflow was equivalent to approximately 5.6% of its starting holdings value. For all the other funds combined, the equivalent was just 1.8%.

In relative terms, BlackRock’s fund experienced roughly three times the withdrawal pressure of its competitors. Its scale explained part of its dominance, but hardly all of it.

The underlying Bitcoin inventory tells a similar story. IBIT held approximately 811,817 BTC on October 30. By November 20, that had fallen to roughly 760,926 BTC, a reduction of nearly 50,900 BTC or 6.3%.

Bitcoin’s declining price could reduce the dollar value of those holdings, but it could not account for the disappearance of the coins themselves. IBIT’s inventory had genuinely contracted.

The departures were measurable. The identities of those departing were another matter.

A $4 billion ETF outflow makes it tempting to declare that institutional investors are abandoning Bitcoin. Yet the available data cannot distinguish an asset manager reducing exposure from an individual investor selling shares, or a market participant unwinding a hedged position.

Nor does it establish whether the capital left Bitcoin altogether or found another route back into the market. That uncertainty matters because the industry has grown comfortable treating ETF inflows as evidence of institutional conviction. Applying the opposite interpretation to withdrawals may be tempting, but it is no more conclusive.

What November demonstrated was a substantial withdrawal of capital from these investment products, led disproportionately by BlackRock’s IBIT.

Whether it represented a broader loss of faith in Bitcoin was a considerably larger question though.

And while investors were heading for the exits, there seemed to be little indication that the fund itself had stopped functioning as intended.

There is an understandable tendency to interpret large ETF outflows as a sign that the investment product itself has somehow failed. However, IBIT’s trading data tells us a more measured story.

According to iShares, IBIT closed at $33.02 on November 20 against a net asset value of $33.05, a discount of about 0.10%. Its 30-day median bid-ask spread was 0.02%. In other words, the fund traded almost exactly at the value of the Bitcoin it holds, even as markets were falling.

Trading was heavy. About 109.2 million IBIT shares changed hands on November 20, more than twice the fund’s 30-day average of about 50.1 million.

That is not the same as money leaving the fund though because trading volume is not net flow. A 30-day median spread also doesn’t show that trading stayed cheap at every volatile moment.

Still, nothing here suggests investors were fleeing a broken product. They were trading a working fund whose underlying asset had dropped sharply. IBIT’s NAV fell $2.08 (5.92%) on November 20 to $33.05, and its NAV total return for 2026 stood at −29.06% as of November 19.

Wall Street made Bitcoin easier to buy. That was never the same promise as making it safer to hold. That distinction matters for the question that comes next — how much of the fall in ETF assets was money leaving, and how much was the price?

According to SoSoValue, combined Spot Bitcoin ETF assets reached approximately $110.8 billion on October 5. By November 20, they had fallen to roughly $71.3 billion.

A decline approaching $39.5 billion sounds extraordinary beside three weeks of approximately $4.14 billion in net withdrawals.

However, assets under management represent the market value of what these funds hold. That value changes both when investors create or redeem shares and when Bitcoin itself rises or falls.

Using Coinbase Bitcoin prices recorded by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, Bitcoin fell from approximately $85,821 on October 5 to $58,831 on November 20 — A fall of 31.4%.

Over the same period, reported ETF assets fell by approximately 36%.

Such a comparison strongly suggests that Bitcoin’s price decline accounted for much of the reduction in ETF asset values. It is not a precise decomposition — flows occurred throughout the period, holdings changed, and the dates and valuation methodologies must be matched before assigning an exact proportion to each driver.

Still, the broad conclusion is difficult to miss.

Tens of billions of dollars can disappear from reported fund asset values without an equivalent sum being withdrawn by investors. A falling portfolio value and a redeemed investment are two different financial events. Treating them interchangeably gives a dramatic headline considerably more authority than it deserves.

Bitcoin’s ETF market was not the only place seeing withdrawals either.

From November 9 to 13, U.S Spot Ether ETFs lost about $398.9 million, according to Farside. BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounted for about $311.1 million of that, or 78%. The following week, Ether funds lost about $306 million, with ETHA responsible for about $230 million or 75%.

That’s the same pattern we saw in Bitcoin — one BlackRock fund carrying most of the headline outflow.

Stablecoins told a slower story. According to DefiLlama, their combined market capitalisation was about $295.3 billion on October 30. It fell to $290.2 billion by November 6, $285.6 billion by November 13, and $281.3 billion by November 20. That is a contraction of about $14 billion, or 4.8%, in three weeks.

Unlike the ETF flows, which peaked in the final week, stablecoins shrank at a fairly steady pace — about $5.1 billion, $4.6 billion, then $4.3 billion a week.

Stablecoins are the dollar-pegged tokens traders use for settlement, trading balances, and collateral. So, a falling supply suggests liquidity may be tightening beyond the regulated ETF market. The two trends overlapped, but they moved at different speeds.

Bitcoin’s own trading schedule adds a complication too.

FRED’s Coinbase series showed Bitcoin falling from about $68,178 on November 13 to $62,891 on November 14, a drop of 7.8%, after that week’s ETF sessions ended.

However, after the much heavier withdrawal week ending November 20, Bitcoin went the other way. It fell from about $58,831 on November 20 to $60,992 on November 22 — A gain of 3.7%.

Two weekends prove nothing on their own, and FRED’s prices are taken at 5 p.m Pacific, not at the ETF close. But they do show that a record ETF outflow and a falling price don’t move in lockstep.

There is no need to minimise the withdrawals. About $4.14 billion in three weeks is a major reversal, particularly when the final week was the worst of the three.

Nor should IBIT’s concentration be brushed off as a consequence of its size. Its 84% share of the net outflows exceeded its roughly two-thirds share of starting industry assets.

However, context changes the interpretation.

SoSoValue’s November 20 figures still showed about $52.8 billion in cumulative net inflows since January 2024. That is down roughly $4 billion from where November began, but nearly three years of accumulated inflows were not erased by three difficult weeks.

October offers a useful warning about reading any headline in isolation. The same fund that masked withdrawals elsewhere in two October weeks went on to account for most of November’s exits. The industry totals recorded both developments accurately, yet told very different stories depending on whether you looked at the funds behind them.

The ETF structure broadened access to Bitcoin. It also gave investors a familiar, liquid way to reduce exposure. Neither is a guarantee about Bitcoin’s price.

Perhaps institutions were cutting risk. Or, retail investors may have been heading for the exits. Others could simply have been unwinding complex positions that had little to do with long-term conviction in Bitcoin. All three are plausible explanations.

What they do establish is narrower but more useful — the withdrawals were substantial, heavily concentrated in one product, and increasingly shared across competing funds as November went on.

So, the next time a billion-dollar ETF outflow makes the headlines, the interesting questions begin after the headline. Which funds accounted for it? How large were the withdrawals relative to their assets? Is the number money leaving a product, or is the market value of its holdings falling?

And one more, which no flow table can answer — Who was actually selling?

#4985. China's Z.ai Says Its New AI Model Can Think Like One Four Times Its Size

China's Z.ai Says Its New AI Model Can Think Like One Four Times Its Size

Chinese AI developer Z.ai released GLM-5.4 on Monday, introducing a new architecture that it claims delivers the reasoning capabilities of models nearly four times its size without requiring nearly as many parameters.

The Beijing-based company says its new 750-billion-parameter model can compete with systems containing two to three trillion parameters. It also supports a one-million-token context window, accepts images and video, and can generate up to 128,000 tokens in a single response, according to its technical documentation. Parameters are the internal values a model learns during training, while tokens are the chunks of text it processes and generates—roughly equivalent to words or parts of words.

The release comes as American companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google dominate the highest positions in AI performance rankings. Chinese developers, meanwhile, have increasingly focused on making powerful models cheaper to run, particularly for coding and autonomous agents.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Z.ai has been among China's strongest competitors. As Decrypt reported in August, its predecessor GLM-5.3 was already competitive with leading American coding models, although it still trailed the best proprietary systems on several software engineering tests.

GLM-5.4 introduces what Z.ai calls a Loop Transformer, which processes information through the same 28 neural network layers twice. Traditional Transformers generally pass information through each layer once, so reusing layers effectively increases computational depth without increasing the number of stored parameters.

The company combines this approach with gated updates, which regulate how much information changes between passes, and a hybrid memory cache that avoids storing an entirely separate copy of previous calculations. Sparse attention also helps the model focus its computing power on relevant information rather than processing everything equally.

In controlled experiments on a smaller 30-billion-parameter model, Z.ai reported that its looping technique increased accuracy on AIME 2025, a mathematics examination benchmark scored by the percentage of correctly solved problems, from 19.17% to 30.42%.

GPQA Diamond, a graduate-level science question-answering test also scored by correct-answer percentage, improved from 47.58% to 56.26%. The experiments required approximately 10% additional training compute, while reducing generated reasoning tokens by 10% to 14% on several tests.

Those results concern the experimental architecture, not independently established performance for GLM-5.4 itself. Z.ai has not published a comprehensive flagship benchmark comparison demonstrating that the new model matches Claude or GPT.

The company is also promoting what it calls Generalized Coding: using programming to accomplish tasks beyond software development. Its demonstrations include building a video game, creating 3D environments, and designing a six-axis robotic arm using engineering software.

The company's previous flagship costs $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens through its API. By comparison, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol costs $2 and $10, while Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 costs $4 and $20, respectively.

At those published rates, GLM-5.3 is considerably cheaper than its American counterparts, although GLM-5.4's own API pricing has not been announced. Its actual performance-per-dollar advantage therefore cannot yet be calculated.

China has other serious contenders. Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max recently topped Chinese competitors on Arena's agent leaderboard, while Moonshot's Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 have challenged American developers on coding performance and API pricing.

The performance gap remains contested. A U.S. government evaluation placed DeepSeek roughly eight months behind the American frontier, although researchers questioned its methodology.

Z.ai itself remains on the U.S. Commerce Department's Entity List, following its January 2025 designation over concerns that its AI research could support Chinese military modernization. The restrictions limit access to controlled American technology, but have not stopped the company from releasing new models.

Zcash holders just got a new update as the major crypto exchange Gemini has announced support for Shielded Zcash deposits.

Scott Merkel, 'Wolf of All Streets,' shared this update in an X post, highlighting the milestone as the first of its kind for any major exchange. According to Merkel, Gemini now lets customers deposit Zcash (ZEC) to shielded addresses, saying it is the first major exchange with both shielded deposits and withdrawals.

GEMINI NOW LETS CUSTOMERS DEPOSIT ZCASH $ZEC TO SHIELDED ADDRESSES, SAYING IT IS THE FIRST MAJOR EXCHANGE WITH BOTH SHIELDED DEPOSITS AND WITHDRAWALS https://t.co/d9pIFJ6uJM

Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss shared the milestone in a recent X post, adding that the recent move builds on the launch of shielded Zcash withdrawals on Gemini this summer.

In July 2026, shortly after the Ironwood upgrade was activated, Gemini launched support for shielded Zcash withdrawals to the new Ironwood pool, allowing users to send Zcash from Gemini to their Ironwood deposit address. Ironwood (NU6.3) went live on July 28, 2026, at block height 3,428,143, bringing a new shielded pool for Zcash.

With the recent launch of support for Shielded Zcash deposits, Gemini users can make Shielded Zcash deposits and withdrawals to and from Ironwood, with Winklevoss remarking that the private movement of money was now complete.

Zcash's total shielded supply now sits at around 4.93 million ZEC (around 28.94% of total ZEC supply) as of November 25, 2026.

November has brought in key updates for the Zcash network. Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live earlier in November 2026, slashing ZEC's target block time to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The new 25-second block target lets miners add a batch of transactions to the chain three times as often.

None of this prints extra ZEC. Each block pays a third as much and halvings come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving.

Days after the NU7 upgrade, the Zcash Foundation followed up with the release of Zebra 7.1.0, which fixed ten security advisories, most of which closed off ways in which another node on the network (a peer) could stop a Zebra node from catching up with the chain or make it run out of memory. It also added sync and memory diagnostics, automatic peer recovery, and clearer errors.

#4983. Fidelity Crypto Adds AAVE, LINK, UNI, Expanding Asset List to Eight

Home » Blitz news » Fidelity Crypto Adds AAVE, LINK, UNI, Expanding Asset List to Eight

Fidelity Investments adds three DeFi tokens to its retail lineup.

Fidelity Investments has added AAVE, Chainlink (LINK) and Uniswap (UNI) to its Fidelity Crypto trading service, expanding its supported digital asset list from five to eight. The addition lifts the number of supported assets from five to eight and brings three DeFi tokens to eligible US customers.

Fidelity announced the update on its official website and in an X post. The platform now supports Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), Litecoin (LTC), AAVE, LINK, UNI and the Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD), a US dollar-pegged stablecoin the company announced in January 2026.

Each new token is tied to a different part of DeFi. AAVE is the token for Aave, a lending protocol that mediates cryptocurrency lending and borrowing.

UNI is the governance token for Uniswap, a decentralized exchange. LINK is used in Chainlink, an oracle network that delivers external information such as price data to smart contracts.

Trading and custody are handled by Fidelity Digital Assets, a subsidiary licensed as a U.S. National Trust Bank. The service is available to eligible U.S. customers aged 18 and over residing in states where Fidelity provides the service.

Fidelity launched Fidelity Crypto for individual investors in 2022, initially offering Bitcoin and Ether. The latest addition follows Charles Schwab’s November 9 listing of Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink on its spot crypto platform.

Fidelity’s addition of AAVE, UNI and LINK extends a major US brokerage’s retail crypto offering to DeFi infrastructure tokens. It also adds to competition among traditional brokerages for crypto-active customers, following Schwab’s recent expansion.

#4981. Bitcoin has fallen so far that its original Rainbow Chart has run out of colors

Bitcoin’s drop below $59,000 exposes the limitations of a valuation model built on historical price trends.

On BlockchainCenter's original Bitcoin Rainbow Chart, the price marker sat below the bottom purple band, and the chart labeled the reading “Bitcoin is dead,” as Bitcoin traded below $59,000 on Nov. 25.

On the same date, BlockchainCenter’s dynamic version displayed “BUY!”

The two readings describe the same selloff from different starting points. BlockchainCenter presents the original and dynamic charts separately, and each version measures Bitcoin against its own curve.

The original chart snapshot uses a fixed formula dating to 2014, while the dynamic chart fits its curve to daily Bitcoin prices starting in 2012.

The colored bands show where the price sits relative to each model’s estimate of its long-term trend. As the original curve rises over time, it takes a higher dollar price to reach the same band.

The dynamic model’s estimate can also change as new price history comes in, and the apparent instructions in the labels take their meaning from the curve each chart uses.

BlockchainCenter puts Bitcoin’s price against two different trends.

A price below the bands on the original chart can coexist with a buy label on the dynamic chart.

Publisher readings for November 25, 2026.

Schematic bands compare BlockchainCenter’s two published readings for November 25, 2026. The displayed dollar value belongs to the original chart snapshot.

Publisher readings for November 25, 2026.

BlockchainCenter’s weekly archive shows that the same “Bitcoin is dead” label was recorded for $74,382 on Nov. 8, $65,118 on Nov. 15, and $60,944 on Nov. 22.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

The Nov. 25 digest also showed it, with Bitcoin below $59,000, and the label had already appeared at weekly checkpoints in May and October.

The November readings capture prices on specific dates, so they leave room for swings in between. Bitcoin can keep falling after the original chart runs out of colors, since the quoted prices capture changes the label obscures once the old chart reaches its lower limit.

In March 2020, Bitcoin briefly slipped below the chart’s lowest band during the pandemic crash, according to BlockchainCenter’s history.

It broke the old boundary again in 2022 when the price fell below $20,000. After the second break, BlockchainCenter added a band beneath its previous floor. The original formula stayed in place, and the new indigo band was labeled “1BTC = 1BTC.”

BlockchainCenter’s creator says the added band also came under pressure, so the site revised the formula in a separate V2 release on Nov. 21, 2022, using more price history to fit a new curve.

Adding a band changed how the old chart displayed low prices, and refitting the curve changed the benchmark itself. Either change could put a price that had fallen outside the old bands on the chart, even before a recovery.

The fourth Bitcoin halving in April 2024 cut the block subsidy to 3.125 BTC, offering a starting point for comparing the rally that followed with the original curve.

Bitcoin went on to set a dollar record, reaching about $126,200 on Oct. 6, 2025. Even that rally stayed short of the yellow and red bands in the portion of the original chart shown in the Nov. 25 snapshot.

Bitcoin recovered from the March 2020 shock and went on to trade well above its 2022 lows. Those recoveries show how different the market can look after a break.

In November, the original chart’s label stayed in place as the price fell, while the dynamic chart put it in a band labeled “BUY!” BlockchainCenter describes the Rainbow Chart as a way to view long-term price history.

The chart’s creator presents even the updated fit as a way to put past price moves in context.

Trump Says He 'Made the Deal' to Reinstate Jensen Huang, Sparking Bipartisan Backlash

U.S. President Donald Trump has taken credit for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, drawing criticism from lawmakers in both parties who say the administration has yet to explain what assurances it gave the company's board.

"I convinced them," Trump told CNBC in a phone interview on Monday, shortly after Nvidia reinstated Huang as president and CEO. "I made the deal."

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Trump said the board had asked for assurances that Huang was not a national security threat, and that the administration provided them based on "everything we know." He said a government investigation had found that Huang himself was exonerated. Asked whether last week's stock losses had shaped his view, Trump said "probably so."

The board's decision was sealed by a personal promise from Trump on Sunday, CNBC reported, citing three people familiar with its thinking. Senior administration officials had contacted directors overnight on Friday, and Huang then joined meetings with the board over the weekend, the outlet said. The board's statement cited input from "senior levels of the United States government" without naming anyone.

Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Saturday that Huang was not the target or subject of any Justice Department investigation, and that there was no evidence he had broken laws, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials.

During a marathon board session on Sunday, Huang disclosed additional affairs beyond the two that had been widely reported, but was contrite, the newspaper said, citing people familiar with the discussion.

Trump told The New York Times that he had consulted Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton before recommending Huang's return. "I had to go to them before I recommended this," he said. A day earlier, Clayton had said that the U.S. investigation into Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, was ongoing.

The reversal came six days after board chair Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to bring Huang back. Trump later posted an AI-generated image on Truth Social showing Huang holding a red bra aloft in his raised fist, in a pose modeled on the photo of Trump after the 2024 assassination attempt on his life.

Huang's reinstatement drew the ire of lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement. She called on the administration to explain what input was given, and by which officials.

Republicans also pushed back. Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR), chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, tweeted that the controversy over Nvidia and Megaspeed was "not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back," and pledged to pass chip export-control bills including his Chip Security Act.

I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access. The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back.…

— Tom Cotton (@SenTomCotton) November 23, 2026

"No national security risk? Based on what?" Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) tweeted, quoting the board's statement. Sen. John Curtis (R-UT) asked who in government had weighed in and what they told the board, noting that it had ruled out Huang's return only a week earlier. "I'd like to know what changed," he wrote.

Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) tweeted that Huang's behavior "does not support reinstatement," adding that Nvidia still had to answer for national security concerns and "unaccounted-for chips."

Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), who is expected to become House Speaker in January, called the board's decision "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible" in a statement. He promised an investigation into Nvidia and into what he called "corrupt abuse of power" by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his department.

Trump's own Nvidia holdings may have gained as much as $15 million in value on Monday, according to the Financial Times, which calculated that he could have held up to 370,000 shares as of September 30, based on his latest ethics disclosure. At the low end of the disclosure's ranges, he would have held about 32,000 shares and gained $1.3 million. The White House did not respond to the newspaper's request for comment.

Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) tweeted that the president was "selling out our national security to keep the stock market high," calling for an investigation into stock trades made before the announcement.

Nvidia shares closed up 31.5% at $165.05 on Monday, adding about $950 billion to its market value, before slipping 5% to $156.82 in premarket trading on Tuesday, according to Yahoo! Finance.

Huang is due to sit for a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 1, and to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3. On Monday, the Commerce Department also added Megaspeed to its Entity List trade blacklist.
